Read ARI/NMI/purity and used units; QE/EV/TE/KL only within one representation (QE is not comparable across feature spaces: say so in the table). Win: ARI falls by less than 0.05 from 0 to 45 degrees for (ii) and (iii) while the raw map falls more, on 8 of 10 seeds; (iii) keeps the mirrored pair apart (purity on that pair above 0.9) where (ii) merges it. On PD: per-item z-scoring must lose ARI on 8 of 10 seeds, confirming loudness as a cue.
ideas.cost: Negligible; one R preprocessing function.
anchors: Bulling, Blanke & Schiele (2014), ACM Computing Surveys, 'A tutorial on human activity recognition using body-worn inertial sensors'
Kunze & Lukowicz (2008), 'Dealing with sensor displacement in motion-based onbody activity recognition systems' (unverified)
Um et al. (2017), ICMI, data augmentation of wearable sensor data (rotation as a nuisance)
ideas.already_tested: partly: z-normalised DTW was tested (no gain in general, one win on solar curves) but it aligned z-scores while averaging raw values on single-channel sets; z-scoring the items themselves, magnitude and the gravity frame were not
ideas.risk: Magnitude discards direction: where direction is the class (up vs down swipe) it loses badly, which the mirrored pair is there to show; the gravity frame needs gestures long enough for the mean acceleration to be gravity; with a fixed sensor (0 degrees) all of this is a wash.
ideas.expected_gain: large on ARI when orientation varies by 15 degrees or more; none when the sensor is fixed; on PD the amplitude arm is expected to show a loss for normalisation, which is the useful number
ideas.problems: The headline test is circular: the session's synthetic gesture generator applies a random axis rotation by construction (rotation_deg, default 35), and |a| is exactly invariant to it, so the win on synthetic data at 45 degrees is guaranteed and proves nothing about the map. The only evidence that counts is real 3-axis data with unknown orientation variance (UWave) and the PD amplitude arm. 'Wiimote sets recorded at varying orientations' is unverified and irrelevant to the project's single-axis cuts (GesturePebbleZ1, ShakeGestureWiimoteZ), where neither |a| nor a gravity frame can be computed. The gravity frame requires gestures that start and end at rest (mean acceleration = gravity only when net velocity change is zero); the synthetic generator does not guarantee that. On PD, the loudness-is-a-cue result is already half in hand: the demonstrator's cosine and correlation distances remove amplitude, and its detection test shows a Euclidean corona AUROC below 0.5 because corona is quiet. Partly tested, as stated: z-normalised DTW aligned z-scores but averaged raw values.
ideas.corrections: Keep it as a cheap preprocessing matrix, not as a SOM improvement. Count only UWave (real) and the PD amplitude rows as evidence; report the synthetic rotation rows as a sanity check, labelled as such. Add 'items z-scored per item' to the PD arm next to the demonstrator's cosine/correlation maps so the loudness question is closed once, with ARI and the per-class detection AUROC. State in the table that QE/EV/KL are not comparable across representations (the idea already does). References: Bulling, Blanke & Schiele (2014) ACM Computing Surveys 46(3), plausible; Kunze & Lukowicz (2008) UbiComp, plausible; Um et al. (2017) ICMI, plausible.

ideas.title: Open-begin / open-end DTW for sloppily segmented gestures
ideas.lens: movement / gesture / HAR from wearable sensors
ideas.what_it_changes: The DTW boundary condition: the path may start anywhere in the first p L samples of the item and end anywhere in the last p L (OBE-DTW), the cost being the minimum over those ends; in the update only matched prototype points are pulled, with a weak pull on unmatched ones so prototypes do not shrink. p is a share like the band.
ideas.mechanism: Cut from a stream by an energy threshold, a gesture carries 0-30% rest at each end; standard DTW must match that rest to the prototype's first and last points, paying a cost that depends on how much rest was included rather than on the gesture, so one class splits across units by pad length. Open ends make the cost depend on the gesture alone. The plain fix (trim by threshold) is brittle at low signal-to-noise.
ideas.why_pd: Onsets are trigger-aligned (open-begin not needed), but the tail is a decay ending at an arbitrary point within 250 us; an open end lets a short corona pulse match the start of a longer prototype without paying for the tail. The decay is a class cue, though, so the test decides whether the freedom helps (void vs corona, different rise and decay) or hurts (the air gap's reflection 50-90 us after onset must still count).
ideas.why_movement: Segmentation slop is the rule in streaming use; this is exactly the rehabilitation case the OE-DTW paper was written for.
ideas.control: The standard DTW-SOM on the same padded items (same seeds); the standard DTW-SOM on items trimmed by the energy threshold (the plain fix).
ideas.how_to_test: Synthetic gestures and GesturePebbleZ1 / ShakeGestureWiimoteZ, each padded on both sides with random rest of 0-30% of L (low-amplitude noise, with the gravity offset for the synthetic set); pd_acoustic with p on the tail only. p in {0, 10%, 30%}. Maps 4x4, 7x7, 10x10; 10 seeds. Read ARI/NMI/purity (own), QE judged with standard DTW on the trimmed items (a fair fit measure), TE/KL (own), a prototype pad share (fraction of each prototype's length below the energy threshold), alignments. Win: ARI on padded items within 0.03 of the ARI on clean items on 8 of 10 seeds while the standard DTW-SOM loses more, and at least the trimmed control's ARI.
ideas.cost: The same DP table; a minimum over the last row and column and a start offset; the update must know the matched range. Small C++ change.
anchors: Tormene, Giorgino, Quaglini & Stefanelli (2009), Artificial Intelligence in Medicine 45:11-34, 'Matching incomplete time series with dynamic time warping: an algorithm and an application to post-stroke rehabilitation' (OE-DTW, OBE-DTW)
The dtw R package (Giorgino) open.begin / open.end options as a reference implementation
ideas.already_tested: no
ideas.risk: With open ends a short item can match a fragment of any prototype, making prototype prefixes attractors, so the free share must be capped; prototypes can shorten if unmatched points never move; on clean UCR cuts it is a wash.
ideas.expected_gain: large on padded or stream-cut gestures; wash on clean cuts; uncertain on PD (the decay cue may be lost)
ideas.problems: The decisive detail is missing: how the partial-match cost is normalised. Raw open-end cost over fewer matched cells favours short prefixes, so prototype prefixes become attractors (the idea notes this but gives no fix); dividing by matched length pushes the other way, and the project's own growing_vs_classic Section 4 showed that DTW divided by path length makes series drift to long prototypes, raises TE, and badly hurt ShakeGestureWiimoteZ ARI. Padding clean UCR cuts with synthetic rest favours any open-end method by construction, so the trimmed-by-threshold control must get the same tuning effort and the fair test is whether OBE-DTW matches the CLEAN-cut ARI, which the win criterion does state. The PD arm is the wrong tool: records are 125 trigger-aligned samples, decay length is a class cue, and the 10% band already gives the tail slack; an open end there is more likely to merge corona and void. The 'weak pull on unmatched prototype points' is a new knob without a stated value. Not already tested: correct.
ideas.corrections: Specify and test two normalisations: (a) cost per matched cell plus a fixed penalty per unmatched point, (b) raw cost with the free share capped at p; report winner-length / item-length and the prototype pad share, as growing_vs_classic Section 4 did, so attractor behaviour is visible. Drop the PD arm or reduce it to one row with open-end on the tail only. Use real stream-cut gestures if the researcher has any; synthetic padding is a sanity check, not evidence. References: Tormene, Giorgino, Quaglini & Stefanelli (2009) Artificial Intelligence in Medicine 45(1):11-34, verified; dtw R package open.begin/open.end (Giorgino 2009, J. Stat. Software), verified.

ideas.title: A map that keeps learning: the growing DTW-SOM as a stream learner with births, deaths and per-unit rates
ideas.lens: movement / gesture / HAR from wearable sensors
ideas.what_it_changes: The growing DTW-SOM's schedule and growth rule: no global clock. Each unit has its own learning rate alpha_k = max(alpha_min, 1 / (1 + n_k)) with n_k its win count discounted by a slow forgetting factor; the radius floats as now; growth continues past the nominal size when a unit's accumulated error passes a threshold (birth from the data, as now); a rim unit that has not won in T items is removed.
ideas.mechanism: The project's maps train for 20 passes on a decaying schedule and then freeze: right for a benchmark, wrong for a smartwatch that meets new gestures and drifting users. Count-based per-unit rates make each prototype the running (DBA-like) mean of its recent items, so the map tracks drift; births from the data give a new class its own unit mid-stream; deaths free units. Failure addressed: a frozen map assigns a new class to the nearest old unit for ever.
ideas.why_pd: PD monitoring is a stream by nature (hours of pulses, new defect types appearing as insulation ages): the same mechanism gives a new discharge type its own unit and shows it as a birth, an event worth flagging in its own right.
ideas.why_movement: Online personalisation and new gestures without retraining.
ideas.control: The fixed DTW-SOM with the standard schedule retrained from scratch on each window of the stream (the plain rival with the same number of alignments); the project's growing DTW-SOM frozen at nominal size.
ideas.how_to_test: A stream built from the synthetic gestures or PD pulses: classes 1-3 for the first 60%, class 4 appearing at 60%, plus a slow drift (mean speed profile shifting by 20% over the stream). 10 seeds; nominal 5x5 with growth caps at 7x7 and 10x10. Read ARI/NMI/purity on the last 20% of the stream, used units and births/deaths over time (plot), QE and TE on sliding windows, alignments. Win: ARI on the last window higher than the frozen map on 8 of 10 seeds and not lower than retraining from scratch at fewer alignments; the new class gets at least one unit of purity above 0.8 on 8 of 10 seeds.
ideas.cost: Moderate: the growing core exists; add per-unit counters, deaths and lattice bookkeeping for removed units (map distances and links recomputed; map_ways already handles links). Runtime like the growing map.
anchors: Fritzke (1995), NIPS, Growing Neural Gas (edge ages and unit removal)
Alahakoon, Halgamuge & Srinivasan (2000), IEEE TNN, GSOM (accumulated-error births)
Berglund & Sitte (2006), IEEE TNN 17(2):305-316, 'The parameterless self-organizing map algorithm'
Der et al. (1996) as cited by the project for the floating radius
ideas.already_tested: partly: the growing DTW-SOM stops at nominal size under the global schedule; 'removing idle units' and 'a stop rule' were listed and never tested; no streaming test exists
ideas.risk: Count-based rates freeze old units exactly as the schedule did unless the forgetting factor is tuned, and that factor is a new knob with the schedule's role; deaths can tear the lattice (the project's tearing lesson: a torn map never won), so restrict deaths to rim units or fill the hole from a neighbour; drift tracking and class finding pull against each other, so judge on the last window and on the whole stream separately.
ideas.expected_gain: large on late-class ARI (the frozen map cannot do it at all); unknown on order
ideas.problems: The neighbourhood in a stream is unspecified, and it is the hard part: if the radius stays at the growing map's 1 the map stays blurred for ever; if it decays there is the global clock again; 'floats as now' only widens where folded. Four new knobs appear (forgetting factor, birth threshold, death horizon T, alpha_min), each with the schedule's role, which is the chaos/tearing pattern unless each gets a stated reason and a sweep. Deaths on a lattice leave holes (the project's tearing lesson), so rim-only deaths are mandatory, not optional. Attribution: the count-based rate 1/(1+n_k) is MacQueen's online k-means / frequency-sensitive learning (Ahalt et al. 1990; DeSieno 1988, which the demonstrator already has as 'conscience', a different mechanism), not Berglund & Sitte's PLSOM, whose rate is error-driven. The closer prior art is Growing When Required (Marsland, Shapiro & Nehmzow 2002, Neural Networks 15:1041-1058, unverified), which already combines births on error, habituation counters and removal. The PD stream claim is reasonable in principle but the lab data are trigger-cut; the stream must be synthesised. Partly tested, as stated.
ideas.corrections: Fix the radius rule before anything else (e.g. per-unit floating radius with a floor of 0.5 and no global decay) and say why. Add the cheapest rival that does the same job: the frozen growing DTW-SOM plus a novelty threshold on distance-to-winner (3 sigma of the unit's own QE) that buffers novel items and triggers one birth; the streaming map must beat THAT on late-class ARI, not only the fully frozen map. Keep retrain-from-scratch per window at equal alignments as the second control. Restrict deaths to rim units; judge last window and whole stream separately as proposed. References: Fritzke (1995) NIPS 7, plausible; Alahakoon, Halgamuge & Srinivasan (2000) IEEE TNN 11(3):601-614, plausible; Berglund & Sitte (2006) IEEE TNN 17(2):305-316, real but misattributed for the count-based rate; Der et al. (1996) as in the project.

ideas.title: The 1-NN DTW ceiling, and an LVQ finishing pass that moves prototypes to class borders
ideas.lens: movement / gesture / HAR from wearable sensors
ideas.what_it_changes: Adds a supervised measure and a supervised finishing step. (a) Report 1-NN DTW held-out accuracy on every series set next to the map's unit-label accuracy (an item is classified by the majority class of its winner, labels fitted on the training half). (b) After unsupervised training, a short LVQ1 pass with DTW: the winner moves towards the item if its label matches, away along the warped pull if not; small alpha, neighbourhood off, lattice positions kept.
ideas.mechanism: 1-NN DTW is the template-matching baseline every time-series classifier is measured against; a SOM is a compressed template set (K prototypes against N items) and should approach it at K/N of the test-time alignments. Where it falls short, the reason is that SOM prototypes sit at density centres, not at class borders; gun vs point differ by small bumps at the ends, where LVQ places the border. Failure addressed: the map's purity ceiling when classes overlap.
ideas.why_pd: Four classes with ambient noise and quiet corona overlapping in loudness: the border is where the information is, and LVQ on the asinh waveforms sharpens it. The 1-NN DTW number also tells the user whether a SOM classifier is worth having on PD at all, which no report has shown.
ideas.why_movement: uWave classified Wiimote-like accelerometer gestures with DTW templates; the 1-NN number says how close the map comes to that with K templates instead of N.
ideas.control: The untouched map's unit-label accuracy (same map, no LVQ pass); 1-NN DTW on all training items (the ceiling); 1-NN DTW on K random training items (the same-budget template baseline).
ideas.how_to_test: GunPoint, GesturePebbleZ1, ShakeGestureWiimoteZ, pd_acoustic, synthetic gestures; stratified 50/50 train/test splits x 10 seeds (the project has only used all items unsupervised; accuracy needs a held-out half). Maps 4x4, 7x7, 10x10. Read accuracy with a confidence interval (new), plus purity/ARI/NMI and QE/TE/KL before and after the LVQ pass (LVQ raises QE and TE: report by how much), and test-time alignments (K against N). Win: SOM plus LVQ within 3 points of 1-NN DTW on 8 of 10 seeds at no more than K/N of the test-time alignments, and above the untouched map on 8 of 10 seeds.
ideas.cost: 1-NN: N^2 alignments once per set, cheap with the project's LB_Keogh; LVQ: one or two passes. Small implementation: the move-away step is the warped pull with a negative sign.
anchors: Kohonen (2001), Self-Organizing Maps, 3rd ed., ch. 6 (LVQ1)
Bagnall, Lines, Bostrom, Large & Keogh (2017), Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery, 'The great time series classification bake off' (1-NN DTW as the baseline)
Liu, Zhong, Wickramasuriya & Vasudevan (2009), Pervasive and Mobile Computing, uWave (DTW templates for accelerometer gestures; unverified details)
ideas.already_tested: no: LVQ is on the never-tested list and no 1-NN number appears in any report
ideas.risk: LVQ degrades the map (QE, TE up) and needs labels, which the user's unsupervised framing has avoided; 150 PD items per class leave small test halves, so report intervals; if the untouched map already reaches 1-NN, LVQ is a wash.
ideas.expected_gain: moderate on accuracy; the 1-NN ceiling is the main value, a number the project never had
ideas.problems: The same-budget baseline is too weak: 1-NN on K RANDOM training items is easy to beat; the honest rival for K supervised templates is K per-class DBA (or medoid) templates with 1-NN DTW (Petitjean et al. 2016, which L11 cites), and a map plus LVQ that cannot beat that has no claim as a template set. The missing anchor is the project's own: Somervuo & Kohonen (1999), Neural Processing Letters 10(2):151-159, 'Self-organizing maps and learning vector quantization for feature sequences', which already defines LVQ with DTW on sequences (the move-away step along the warped pull is theirs, not new). Adding held-out accuracy changes the project's protocol (all items unsupervised, ARI from a Ward cut); with 150 PD items per class the test halves give 75 per class, so intervals are needed (the idea says so). LVQ's effect on QE/TE is predictable (both worse) and is not a finding. Not already tested: LVQ is on the never-tested list and no 1-NN number exists, correct. The value lies in the ceiling and in the K-vs-N test-time cost framing, which is the right one for a smartwatch or a PD monitor.
ideas.corrections: Add the per-class DBA-template 1-NN baseline at the same K and cite Somervuo & Kohonen (1999) as the source of DTW-LVQ. Report accuracy with a binomial interval and the K/N alignment ratio; keep purity/ARI/NMI and QE/TE before and after LVQ as proposed. Run the 1-NN ceiling first on every set; only where the untouched map is more than 3 points below it is the LVQ pass worth its seeds. References: Kohonen (2001) 3rd ed. ch. 6, verified; Bagnall, Lines, Bostrom, Large & Keogh (2017) DMKD 31(3):606-660, plausible; Liu, Zhong, Wickramasuriya & Vasudevan (2009) Pervasive and Mobile Computing 5(6):657-675, plausible.

ideas.title: Trustworthiness and continuity (plus the co-ranking curve): item-level order at a chosen scale, immune to the map outline
ideas.what_it_changes: A new scorer takes the map table plus the N x N item distance matrix (Euclid or DTW). Each item gets map coordinates (its winner's cell centre, ties among items on one unit broken by average ranks or by distance to the winner), neighbours are ranked in data space and on the map, and T(k), C(k) are computed for k = 1..N/10, together with the co-ranking matrix and its Q_NX(k) curve.
ideas.mechanism: T(k) = 1 - 2 / (N k (2N - 3k - 1)) * sum_i sum_{j in U_k(i)} (r_data(i,j) - k), where U_k(i) are items among i's k map-nearest that are not among its k data-nearest; C(k) mirrors it with data-neighbours missing from the map neighbourhood and map ranks. T punishes folds (far items brought together: the map lies), C punishes tears (data neighbours split apart). TE only asks whether the two best units of an item touch; TP compares whole rank lists of prototypes and reacts to map outline and data curvature, which is why the project could not decide whether to believe it on grown maps. T/C work on items at a fixed scale k, so an irregular outline costs nothing, and because k is relative to N the numbers are comparable across map sizes. The T-vs-C split is also the fit/order tension seen from the item side: a tearing map that breaks a real gap should raise T; one that shreds a random start should drop C; this tests directly why tearing never beat a smaller start radius.
ideas.why_pd: A fold that puts a void discharge next to ambient noise on the map is exactly what a technician would misread; T at k ~ 10 measures that.
ideas.why_movement: Gestures that are variations of one another should stay contiguous on a map used as a gesture dictionary; C at k ~ 10 measures that.
ideas.control: TE and KL read together, and TP. The measure earns its place if it sides with TE/KL on the known trade-offs (batch SOM: fit up, order down; CHAOSOM: the reverse) and gives a verdict on the growing SOM that does not change when the outline is regularised (compare the grown map with a plain map restricted to the same set of used units).
ideas.how_to_test: All 14 benchmark variants at the default size from the cache (only the N x N distances and the map tables are needed), plus plain and growing maps at 4x4..12x12, 10 seeds, on PD, CBF, GunPoint. Read T(k), C(k) at k = 5, 10, 20 and Q_NX. Win = (i) agreement with TE/KL on batch and CHAOSOM on most seeds, (ii) a stable growing-map verdict under outline control, (iii) on the tearing lab, C falls on the shredded low-threshold maps while T rises on the three-blob set. Table: T and C columns with a k slider; T-vs-C scatter per variant with size as colour; Q_NX(k) curves with a variant dropdown.
ideas.cost: N x N distances (already computed for DTW judging; Euclid trivial) and N sorts of length N: 600^2 for PD, well under a second; the CRAN package coRanking builds the matrix.
anchors: Venna & Kaski (2001) Neighborhood preservation in nonlinear projection methods, ICANN 2001 (verified)
Lee & Verleysen (2009) Quality assessment of dimensionality reduction: rank-based criteria, Neurocomputing 72, 1431-1443 (verified)
Bauer & Pawelzik (1992) topographic product, already in the project; Villmann et al. (1997) on its outline sensitivity, already cited
ideas.already_tested: no: TP is the only rank-based measure used, and the benchmark left its disagreement with TE unresolved
ideas.risk: On coarse maps many items share a cell, so ranks tie massively and T/C become noisy below ~20 units (report the tie share). T/C partly measure how clustered the DATA are, so only same-data comparisons are valid, as now. Under DTW the triangle inequality fails and ranks are only heuristically neighbourhoods.
ideas.expected_gain: moderate: a decision on TP vs TE for grown maps and a size-fair order measure; no change to fit verdicts
ideas.problems: Item-level ranks on a map where ~6 items share one cell (600 items, 100 units) are mostly ties inside the cell at k = 5..20, so T(k)/C(k) at small k measure the tie-break rule as much as the map; the idea names the risk but the proposed fix (average ranks or distance to the winner) is ad hoc. T and C are also partly properties of the data (how clustered it is), so they only rank maps on the same data, which is already the project's rule. The outline control as written ('a plain map restricted to the same set of used units') cannot be applied post hoc to a trained plain map.
ideas.corrections: Use Venna & Kaski's own SOM protocol (items placed at their BMU, which they did in the 2001 paper as far as I recall) AND a unit-level version (T/C on the K prototypes with exact lattice coordinates, no ties) and report both plus the tie share. The decisive outline control is a plain SOM trained from a random start on the grown map's FINAL lattice: the core's som_online_cpp takes any lattice distance matrix g, so this is a one-line control, and it is the control the growing-map verdict itself has never had (growth process vs outline). Under DTW, state that ranks are heuristic (no triangle inequality). Keep the win criterion: sides with TE/KL on batch (fit up, order down) and CHAOSOM (reverse) on most seeds, and the grown-map verdict does not flip under the same-lattice control.

ideas.title: Let the map choose the number of groups: silhouette / Davies-Bouldin over the prototype tree, ARI at the data-chosen k
ideas.what_it_changes: In the two-level clustering (Ward on used prototypes) the cut is chosen by the silhouette or Davies-Bouldin index over k = 2..10 instead of the true class count; the report shows k_hat, ARI(k_hat), NMI(k_hat) next to ARI at the true k, plus the item silhouette with prototypes as centres as a label-free cluster-quality number (DTW: medoids and the N x N DTW matrix).
ideas.mechanism: s_i = (b_i - a_i) / max(a_i, b_i) with a_i the mean distance to i's own group and b_i to the nearest other group; DB = (1/k) sum_j max_{l != j} (s_j + s_l) / d(c_j, c_l) with s_j the mean spread of group j. The project lists 'ARI and NMI rest on one choice' as a limit; this turns the choice into a measured quantity: does the map's structure, read without labels, reveal the right NUMBER of kinds? k_hat should not depend on K once K >> k, so it is a cross-size sanity check in itself. It catches a map whose ARI at the true k is good only because it was told k.
ideas.why_pd: The field question is how many kinds of discharge are present and whether noise is one of them; the 4-class set gives a known answer to test k_hat against.
ideas.why_movement: Number of distinct gestures in an unlabeled session; the map must not need to be told.
ideas.control: Silhouette-chosen k on the raw items with k-means (Euclid) or k-medoids (DTW), no map; and the current ARI at true k. Win = the map's k_hat hits the true count on more seeds than the no-map rival (sign test), and ARI(k_hat) is within 0.05 of ARI(true k) on most seeds.
ideas.how_to_test: 12 data sets, default size, both distances, 10 seeds; size series on PD, GunPoint, CBF to check that k_hat is flat in K. Table: k_hat, ARI(k_hat), silhouette, DB next to ARI(true k); a dendrogram-cut widget with a k slider that recolours the map.
ideas.cost: Negligible on K <= 100 prototypes; item silhouette under DTW needs the N x N DTW matrix, which exists.
anchors: Rousseeuw (1987) silhouettes (standard; details unverified here)
Davies & Bouldin (1979) (standard; unverified)
Vesanto & Alhoniemi (2000) two-level clustering, already in the project
ideas.already_tested: no: 'choosing number of groups from data' is on the project's never-tested list
ideas.risk: Silhouette prefers few round groups: on Chainlink and on overlapping PD classes it may pick 2; the labels are 'one structure among several' (the project's own caveat), so a miss is not always the map's fault.
ideas.expected_gain: moderate for the PD/movement use; small for variant ranking
ideas.problems: Silhouette on ~100 prototypes is noisy and prefers few round groups (Chainlink, overlapping PD classes: corona vs air gap will likely merge to k_hat = 3), as the idea says. Davies-Bouldin needs centroids and within-group spread; under DTW a medoid stands in, which is fine but should be said. Ward on a DTW dissimilarity is already a heuristic in the project, so the tree itself is not Euclidean-Ward. The labels are 'one structure among several', so a miss on k_hat is not always the map's fault; the no-map rival absorbs that.
ideas.corrections: Compute the silhouette on items (not prototypes), with each item in its winner's group and the N x N distance (Euclid or the existing DTW matrix); report k_hat from silhouette AND from the U-matrix watershed basin count (L3) as two map-side methods against silhouette-chosen k with k-means / PAM on the raw items. Win as stated: sign test over seeds on 'k_hat hits the true count' vs the no-map rival, and ARI(k_hat) within 0.05 of ARI(true k) on most seeds; add the flatness of k_hat in K over the size series as the sanity check. Rousseeuw (1987, J. Comput. Appl. Math. 20) and Davies & Bouldin (1979, IEEE TPAMI) are the standard references.

ideas.title: Detection metrics for PD vs noise: a noise-trained map as a novelty detector with ROC AUC, F1 at a fixed false-alarm rate, false alarms per 1000 triggers
ideas.what_it_changes: A detection scorer: train the map on ambient noise only (later: on all 'normal' data), score every held-out waveform by its distance to the winner d_i (own distance), and report ROC AUC (discharge vs noise), the threshold at the 99th percentile of training-noise d_i, precision/recall/F1 at that threshold and false alarms per 1000 noise triggers (per hour once a field trigger rate is given). A second stage, trained on all four classes with labelled units, gives the same numbers per class pair (void vs corona is the hard one).
ideas.mechanism: AUC = P(d_discharge > d_noise), a rank statistic, so it is size-fair and unit-free; QE is the mean of d over all items and sees nothing of the separation between two groups of items. The detector needs a threshold with a known false-alarm rate, which no current measure gives. Across sizes the curve matters: a bigger noise map lowers d for noise AND for quiet discharges that resemble noise, so AUC vs K should show an optimum rather than a monotone trend, which is a legitimate cross-size result.
ideas.why_pd: It is the PD task. The 4-decade loudness means a plain RMS threshold may already separate noise from discharges, so that must be the first control; the interesting case is the quietest quartile of each discharge class, where loudness fails and waveform shape (ringing, decay) must carry the detection.
ideas.why_movement: The same scorer gives open-set gesture rejection: train on known gestures, hold one out, AUC of d for the unseen gesture.
ideas.control: (1) An RMS / asinh-energy threshold, no map; (2) 1-NN distance to the full training-noise set (the ceiling for 'distance to the nearest noise'); (3) K random noise waveforms as prototypes (size-matched, untrained) and k-means / DTW k-medoids with K centroids. Win = AUC and F1@1% FA above all three on most seeds (sign test), on the full set and on the quietest-quartile subset.
ideas.how_to_test: pd_acoustic, 5-fold split by waveform (by recording session if the Zenodo files carry one); noise-only training with K = 9, 16, 36, 64, 100; 10 seeds; Euclid and DTW; read AUC with bootstrap CI, F1@1% FA, FA/1000, and the ROC. Table: AUC, F1, FA/1000 with dropdowns for training class, distance, size; ROC curves with a size slider and a quietest-quartile toggle.
ideas.cost: K alignments per held-out waveform per map: trivial; the noise-only maps are small and fast.
anchors: Fawcett (2006) An introduction to ROC analysis (unverified details)
Markou & Singh (2003) novelty detection review (unverified)
Havránek et al. (2026) pd_acoustic data, already in the project
ideas.already_tested: no: every current measure is in-sample and four-class; no threshold, no held-out items
ideas.risk: The RMS baseline may win outright, in which case the map's value is classification, not detection; with 150 waveforms per class the AUC CI is about +/-0.03; the recordings are trigger-aligned, so 'noise' items are themselves triggered events and false alarms per hour needs a field trigger rate that the lab data cannot supply.
ideas.expected_gain: large for the application (a usable threshold with a stated false-alarm rate); unknown for ranking variants
ideas.problems: F1 at a 1% false-alarm rate cannot be set from 120 training-noise waveforms (5-fold on 150): the 99th percentile of 120 items is between the largest and second-largest value, so the threshold is pure noise. The noise class was not triggered by a current pulse (there is none), so 'noise' items are a different kind of event than the discharge recordings; the idea notes this but it also means the RMS/asinh-energy control may win outright on the full set, which is why the quietest-quartile subset is the real test. 1-NN to the full noise set is the natural ceiling and a map can only match it on AUC, so the map's claim must be 'same AUC at K alignments' plus the smoothing effect of averaged prototypes, which is a genuine open question. Fawcett (2006, PRL 27) and Markou & Singh (2003, Signal Processing 83) are real as far as I recall.
ideas.corrections: Use FA rates of 5% and 10%, or pool held-out noise scores over the 5 folds before setting the threshold; give bootstrap CIs on AUC pooled over folds (150 vs 450). Add the leave-one-class-out novelty test (map trained on three classes, AUC of distance-to-winner for the held-out fourth class), which is the actual 'new kind of discharge' question and is more decisive than noise-only training. Define the quiet quartile by RMS within each discharge class. Controls stay as written (RMS threshold; 1-NN to training noise; K random noise prototypes; k-means / DTW k-medoids with K centroids), sign test over seeds.

ideas.title: Held-out per-class confusion: the labelled map as a classifier on folds, by actor for movement, by waveform or session for PD
ideas.what_it_changes: A held-out protocol in the runner: stratified 5-fold (GunPoint: leave-one-actor-out; UCR sets: their official train/test split); train on the training fold, label each unit by its majority class (empty units inherit the nearest labelled unit along the lattice), predict the test fold by the winner's label; report the confusion matrix, per-class recall and precision, macro-F1 and balanced accuracy. Purity and ARI remain as in-sample numbers beside them.
ideas.mechanism: Purity rises with units because it is in-sample; held-out accuracy falls when a map overfits, so it is fair across sizes by construction, which removes the project's purity trap. C[a,b] = number of test items of class a predicted b; recall_a = C[a,a] / sum_b C[a,b]; macro-F1 = mean over classes of 2PR/(P+R). Per-class rows show WHICH classes a variant confuses, which a single ARI hides; a cost-weighted version (void read as corona costs more than the reverse) follows directly.
ideas.why_pd: Which discharge type is misread as which is the field question; void discharges are the dangerous ones, so the confusion row for 'void' is the number to watch, and a session-wise split tests transfer to a new recording.
ideas.why_movement: A per-person split (new user) is the real question for gesture recognition; the confusion matrix shows which gestures collide.
ideas.control: 1-NN with the same distance on the training fold (the UCR standard baseline, hard to beat) and a K-centroid classifier (k-means / DTW k-medoids with K = number of units, labelled the same way): the size-matched no-map rival. Win = macro-F1 >= the K-centroid classifier's on most seeds (compression costs no accuracy) and within a stated margin of 1-NN; a variant beats the plain SOM by sign test p < 0.05 on held-out macro-F1.
ideas.how_to_test: pd_acoustic (5-fold), GunPoint (by actor), Synthetic Control and Trace (official splits), CBF; add a true multi-channel movement set, e.g. UWaveGestureLibrary (8 gestures, 3 accelerometer axes, 315 points, UCR archive; Liu et al. 2009, unverified) since the project has no multi-channel data yet; sizes 4x4..12x12; 10 seeds. Table: confusion heatmap with variant/size/fold dropdowns, per-class recall bars, macro-F1 and balanced accuracy next to in-sample purity and ARI to show the in-sample gap.
ideas.cost: The benchmark cache must be rebuilt with folds (the real cost: cached maps were trained on all items); per map, training on 80% of items plus K alignments per test item.
anchors: Dau et al. (2019) UCR archive, already in the project, for splits and 1-NN baselines
Kohonen (2013) on labelled maps and LVQ, already in the project
ideas.already_tested: no: every measure in the five reports is computed on the training items; the map is never used as a classifier
ideas.risk: 1-NN DTW will likely beat every map on accuracy (as the UCR literature shows), so the honest claim is 'accuracy at K prototypes', not 'best classifier'; PD test folds of 120 items give about +/-4 pp noise per class.
ideas.expected_gain: large in meaning (first out-of-sample numbers; removes the purity trap); unknown in ranking changes
ideas.problems: GunPoint 'by actor': the UCR files do not carry per-series actor labels as far as I know (the description mentions two actors, the data give only class), so that split may be impossible; mark doubtful. Rebuilding the cache with folds for all 14 variants is the real cost and most of it is wasted on variants already retired (chaotic units, DTW-for-winner-only, PCA start). 1-NN DTW will beat every map on accuracy, as the idea admits, so the claim is 'accuracy at K prototypes'. Per-class recall on PD is +/-8 pp per fold with 30 test items per class; pooled over 5 folds about +/-4 pp. UWaveGestureLibrary (Liu et al. 2009, Pervasive and Mobile Computing; UEA multivariate version with 3 axes, 315 points, 8 gestures) is correctly described as far as I recall, but it needs the never-tested multi-channel DTW first, which is a map change, not a measure.
ideas.corrections: Restrict the fold rebuild to online SOM, DTW-SOM, growing DTW-SOM and batch SOM (plus widening window if cheap). Use UCR official splits where they exist and repeated stratified 5-fold elsewhere; drop the GunPoint actor split unless the labels can be found. Keep both controls (1-NN with the same distance; K-centroid classifier labelled the same way) and the sign test over seeds on held-out macro-F1. Natural follow-on for the map side: LVQ1 fine-tuning of the labelled SOM (on the never-tested list) with the labelled SOM itself as the control, same folds and seeds. This protocol is also what L6 and L9 need, so it should be built first.

ideas.title: Stability across seeds: ARI between the groupings of different seeds, null-corrected unit-level NMI, per-item wobble on the map
ideas.what_it_changes: From the stored per-seed partitions, score() adds: group stability S_group = mean over the 45 seed pairs of ARI between the two-level groupings (same number of groups); unit stability S_unit = mean NMI between item-to-unit assignments minus the NMI of two random assignments to K units (its size null); and a per-item co-association (share of seed pairs in which two items share a unit), from which an item's wobble = 1 - mean co-association with its usual companions, drawn on the map.
ideas.mechanism: A variant can win on the mean and give a different map every run; the project's 'spread over seeds' is the spread of a number, not of the map. ARI between partitions is size-fair at a fixed group count; unit-level NMI rises with K and needs its null. It catches what the wins table cannot: a 7/10 win with S_group = 0.3 means little; births from data (DTW medoids in the growing map) should be more repeatable than random starts; low-threshold tearing (shredded starts) and chaotic units should be unstable.
ideas.why_pd: A monitor retrained next week must give the same groups; a new ridge must come from the data, not the seed.
ideas.why_movement: A reproducible gesture dictionary across trainings.
ideas.control: Stability of k-means / DTW k-medoids with K centroids over the same seeds (the no-map rival, whose instability is well known), and the plain SOM for variants. Win = S_group of the variant above the plain SOM's with sign test p < 0.05 using seeds as the unit (leave-one-seed-out means), and the SOM above k-means at the same K, a testable claim about neighbourhood smoothing.
ideas.how_to_test: No new training: the benchmark cache (14 variants x 12 sets x 10 seeds) gives 45 pairs per cell; the size series for the plain map adds the K dependence. Table: S_group, S_unit (null-corrected), next to the wins/n columns; a map of item wobble with variant and size dropdowns.
ideas.cost: Zero training; 45 ARI computations per cell, negligible.
anchors: Ben-Hur, Elisseeff & Guyon (2002) stability-based method for discovering structure in clustered data (unverified)
Lange, Roth, Braun & Buhmann (2004) stability-based validation of clustering solutions (unverified)
Hubert & Arabie (1985) ARI, already in the project
ideas.already_tested: partly: the SD of each measure over seeds appears in tooltips; agreement between the maps of different seeds was never computed
ideas.risk: Stability rewards trivial solutions (everything in one unit is perfectly stable), so read next to ARI and QE; the 45 pairs from 10 seeds are not independent, hence the leave-one-seed-out unit for the test.
ideas.expected_gain: moderate: likely to separate born-from-data from random-start variants and to flag tearing and chaotic units; free
ideas.problems: 'Zero training' is wrong: the benchmark cache (`bench`) stores scalar scores per (dataset, variant, seed, eval) plus compared/seconds/used/not_nearest, and the theatres store seed-1 animation frames only; per-item winner tables and the two-level partitions are not cached, so the maps must be retrained (cheap: the whole benchmark was minutes of CPU, but not zero). The unit-level NMI null is better handled by the adjusted mutual information (Vinh, Epps & Bailey 2010, JMLR, unverified) than by subtracting a random-assignment mean. Stability rewards collapsed maps (chaotic units with few used units will look stable), so it must be read next to ARI/used units, as the idea says. The SOM-above-k-means claim is cheap because k-means instability is well known; the informative comparison is variant vs plain SOM. The 45 pairs from 10 seeds are dependent; the leave-one-seed-out device is awkward.
ideas.corrections: Retrain the four or five live variants with the per-item bmu stored (same seeds as the benchmark); use AMI for unit-level agreement and ARI at the true k for group-level; for the test, report the mean pairwise ARI with a bootstrap over seeds, or a permutation test that shuffles variant labels within seed pairs. Keep the per-item co-association wobble map; it is the one output that would show a PD technician which waveforms are assigned unreliably. Ben-Hur, Elisseeff & Guyon (2002, PSB) and Lange et al. (2004, Neural Computation 16) are the standard references.

ideas.title: Distance-to-winner as a confidence: error-detection AUROC, coverage-accuracy curve and calibration error on held-out items
ideas.what_it_changes: For the labelled map of L7, each prediction gets a confidence: the margin m_i = (d_other - d_1) / d_1 with d_1 the distance to the winner and d_other the distance to the nearest unit of a different label (the map table already stores dist and bmu2; bmu2 becomes 'nearest other-label unit'), or a softmax over units p(c | x) proportional to sum over units u with label c of exp(-d(x, m_u)^2 / T), with T fitted on the training fold. Report AUROC of the confidence as a predictor of 'prediction correct', the coverage-accuracy curve (accuracy when abstaining on the least confident x%), and ECE = sum_b (n_b / N) |acc_b - conf_b| over 5-10 bins.
ideas.mechanism: A map that is right 80% of the time is far more useful if it knows which 20% it is wrong on; QE and purity cannot see this. It catches whether the per-item distance carries information at all: in the chaotic-unit maps the winner was not the nearest unit, so d_1 is meaningless; with a wide DTW window every d_1 shrinks and loses contrast (the project's 'a wide window hides the timing'); 'DTW for the winner only' may keep accuracy and still ruin the confidence. AUROC, coverage curves and ECE (with T refitted per map) are size-fair.
ideas.why_pd: Abstention means 'send to a human' or 'mark as a new kind of discharge'; with asinh-scaled pressure the distances are on a readable scale and the quiet air-gap discharges are where the map should confess doubt.
ideas.why_movement: Reject unclear gestures instead of acting on them.
ideas.control: 1-NN with its own distance and class margin as confidence, and the K-centroid classifier's softmax. Win = error-detection AUROC >= both controls on most seeds; ECE < 0.05 after temperature fitting; accuracy at 90% coverage above 1-NN's.
ideas.how_to_test: On the held-out folds of L7; sizes 4x4..12x12; 10 seeds. Table: AUROC(err), ECE, accuracy at 90% coverage; a reliability diagram and a coverage-accuracy curve with variant/size dropdowns; the map coloured by mean margin per unit to show where it is unsure.
ideas.cost: Negligible: d_1 and the second distance exist in the map table; one scalar T per map.
anchors: Guo, Pleiss, Sun & Weinberger (2017) On calibration of modern neural networks, temperature scaling and ECE (unverified)
Hendrycks & Gimpel (2017) max-softmax baseline for error detection (unverified)
ideas.already_tested: no: dist and bmu2 are stored per item but only averaged into QE and TE
ideas.risk: With about 100 test items per class the reliability bins are noisy (use 5 bins and bootstrap CIs); DTW is not a metric, so the softmax is a heuristic; the margin depends on the map's label coverage (dead units).
ideas.expected_gain: moderate for the application; small for variant ranking, but it may expose variants whose accuracy holds while their confidence is empty
ideas.problems: Not a separate experiment: it is two or three extra columns on L7's held-out table and should be presented that way. ECE with temperature scaling is over-built for a prototype classifier with ~100 test items per class (5 bins, each with ~20 items, bins noise of +/-10 pp), and the softmax over units is a heuristic under DTW, as admitted. The 'catches chaotic maps whose d_1 is meaningless' claim is decorative: chaotic units are already retired. The wide-window claim ('every d_1 shrinks') does not bite on a ratio margin; only a loss of contrast would, which is speculative. The map table fields (dist, bmu2) exist in the core's map_cpp output but are not cached, so this rides on L7's rebuild.
ideas.corrections: Report the margin m = (d_other - d_1)/d_1 (nearest other-label unit), error-detection AUROC and accuracy at 90% coverage next to L7's macro-F1, against 1-NN's class margin and the K-centroid classifier's margin; drop ECE and temperature fitting. Colour the map by mean margin per unit (the one PD-relevant picture: where the map should 'send to a human'). Guo et al. (2017, ICML) and Hendrycks & Gimpel (2017, ICLR) are correctly cited as far as I recall.

ideas.title: Honest statistics for seed-by-seed wins: sign test, paired Wilcoxon with Hodges-Lehmann CI, effect size, Holm/FDR, Friedman-Nemenyi, and an equivalence verdict
ideas.what_it_changes: wins_table() and the leaderboard tooltips: each (variant, baseline, data set, measure) cell gets wins/n; the exact two-sided sign-test p; the Wilcoxon signed-rank p on the paired per-seed differences (same seed = same start and item order, a true pairing); the Hodges-Lehmann median difference with 95% CI in the measure's units and in percent; d_z = mean difference / SD of differences; a Holm-adjusted flag within each variant's family (one variant x one measure over data sets) and a Benjamini-Hochberg FDR flag over the whole table; across data sets a Friedman test with a Nemenyi critical-difference diagram per measure in place of the mean scaled rank; and a four-way verdict using the project's own margins (ARI 0.05, TE 0.5 pp, KL 0): better / worse / equivalent (CI inside +/- margin) / undecided.
ideas.mechanism: With 10 seeds the sign test gives p = 0.75 for 6/10, 0.34 for 7/10, 0.11 for 8/10, 0.021 for 9/10, 0.002 for 10/10, so 'won on most seeds' is not evidence and the 80% rule sits at p ~ 0.11 before correction. The benchmark has about 14 x 7 x 12 = 1,176 cells, so about 59 would pass p < 0.05 by chance. The CI on the median difference says whether a win exceeds the smallest difference anyone cares about, which splits the current 'ties or split' into equivalent and undecided. A seed budget follows: for 80% power at alpha 0.05 the paired test needs roughly 8 / d_z^2 seeds (paired-t approximation; Wilcoxon about 5% more), i.e. about 8 seeds for d_z = 1 and about 33 for d_z = 0.5.
ideas.why_pd: The PD gains in ARI are small (0.02-0.05) and would need 30+ seeds to confirm or to call equivalent; better to know that than to report 6/10.
ideas.why_movement: Same for GunPoint, where the class difference lies in small bumps and seed noise is large relative to the effect.
ideas.control: The current 'won on most seeds' count and the '80% of seeds plus a margin' rule. The statistics earn their place if they overturn at least one claimed win or loss in the summary report (expected: several of the 6/10 and 7/10 cells) while the Friedman-Nemenyi ordering agrees with the mean-rank leaderboard on the clear cases (sanity check).
ideas.how_to_test: Re-run wins_table on the cached benchmark (no new maps); then 30 seeds on the three cells nearest the margin (PD: growing DTW-SOM vs DTW-SOM on ARI; CBF: TE; GunPoint: KL) to see whether 'undecided' resolves. Table columns: wins/n, p_sign, p_Wilcoxon, Delta_HL [95% CI], d_z, Holm and FDR flags, verdict; colour a cell only when the CI excludes zero; a critical-difference diagram per measure behind a dropdown.
ideas.cost: Zero compute: wilcox.test(conf.int = TRUE) gives the Hodges-Lehmann estimate and CI, binom.test the sign test, p.adjust Holm and BH; Nemenyi via PMCMRplus or scmamp (CRAN package names from memory, unverified).
anchors: Demšar (2006) Statistical comparisons of classifiers over multiple data sets, JMLR 7, 1-30 (verified)
Wilcoxon (1945); Hodges & Lehmann (1963) (standard; unverified details)
Holm (1979); Benjamini & Hochberg (1995) (standard; unverified details)
Lakens (2017) equivalence tests / TOST (unverified)
ideas.already_tested: partly: wins on most seeds, the 80%-plus-margin rule, and a mean scaled rank across data sets; no p-values, CIs, effect sizes or corrections anywhere
ideas.risk: Ten seeds give low power, so many cells turn 'undecided' and the summary looks weaker (the honest outcome); seeds vary only start and order, so the CI is about training noise, not about new data (the project's own caveat); Holm over 1,000+ tests is very conservative, hence per-family Holm plus FDR.
ideas.expected_gain: large in credibility at zero cost; it will probably retract some claimed wins and reclassify most ties
ideas.problems: The equivalence verdict cannot work for KL with the project's margin of 0: a CI inside +/-0 is impossible, so KL cells can only be better/worse/undecided; a relative margin (e.g. 1-2% of the baseline's KL) is needed. Friedman-Nemenyi must run per family (the Euclidean variants compete on 12 sets with 6 maps, the DTW variants on 8 series sets), not over the whole 14-variant table. The seeds vary only start and item order, so all p-values are about training noise, not generalisation, which the idea states. The project's own 'clear win' rule in the growing report is already a count (>= 80% of seeds) plus a margin on the mean, so the honest statistics sharpen rather than replace it. scmamp's CRAN status is uncertain (may be archived); PMCMRplus is on CRAN as far as I recall. The sign-test p-values quoted (0.75, 0.34, 0.11, 0.021, 0.002 for 6..10 of 10) and the 8/d_z^2 seed budget check out.
ideas.corrections: Add a relative margin for KL and QE (the project's relQE scale), run Friedman per family, keep Holm within (variant x measure over data sets) and BH over the table. Then do the proposed 30-seed rerun on the three near-margin cells (PD growing DTW-SOM vs DTW-SOM on ARI; CBF TE; GunPoint KL) and report which 'helps' verdicts in the summary survive. Demšar (2006, JMLR 7), Holm (1979), Benjamini & Hochberg (1995), Hodges & Lehmann (1963), Lakens (2017) are the standard references.

ideas.title: Fit ratio against the best quantiser at the same K (k-means / DTW k-medoids) and a DTW version of explained variance
ideas.what_it_changes: score() gains, per (data, size, seed), the QE of k-means with K centroids (Euclid) or of PAM k-medoids on the N x N DTW matrix (DTW), started from the same random start, and reports the fit gap G = QE_map / QE_quantiser (>= 1; 1 means the map fits as well as a map-free quantiser) and EV_DTW = 1 - mean d_dtw(x, winner)^2 / mean d_dtw(x, global DTW medoid)^2, the EV analogue with a medoid in place of the mean.
ideas.mechanism: QE falls with K because any K points do; G divides that out and reads as 'the price of order' in the same units at every size. The benchmark found batch SOM almost k-means at the end (G ~ 1.0 expected) and online SOM worse in fit (G ~ 1.1-1.3 expected); the growing map's lower QE becomes either a G nearer 1 or not, which settles whether it merely places units where k-means would. EV is already unit-free across data sets but exists only under Euclid because DTW has no mean; the medoid version makes fit comparable across data sets under DTW too. It catches a size whose QE gain is not earned (G rising with K means the map keeps less of what a quantiser could get).
ideas.why_pd: Raw QE in asinh(pressure) units is hard to read; G and EV_DTW are unitless and let the PD results sit next to the other data sets.
ideas.why_movement: Multi-channel sets (accelerometer axes in mixed units) make raw QE meaningless across sets; the ratio survives.
ideas.control: Raw QE and relQE (vs the plain SOM, same size and seed). G earns its place if it is flat in K for the plain SOM (Spearman |rho| < 0.3 over 5 sizes) while raw QE has rho = -1, and if the variant ranking at the default size is unchanged.
ideas.how_to_test: Size series 4x4..12x12 on PD, CBF, GunPoint, Synthetic Control, both distances, 10 seeds; k-means with 10 restarts; PAM on the N x N DTW matrix (one matrix per data set, reused for all variants, seeds and sizes). Table: QE | G | EV (Euclid) | EV_DTW with a size dropdown; plot of G vs K per variant, the price-of-order curve.
ideas.cost: k-means negligible; the N x N DTW matrix once per data set (PD: 180k alignments, seconds in Rcpp); PAM on 600 items negligible.
anchors: Kaufman & Rousseeuw (1990) PAM (unverified details)
Petitjean, Ketterlin & Gançarski (2011) DBA, already in the project (the stronger but costlier ceiling)
the project's own k-means control and aweSOM-style EV
ideas.already_tested: partly: k-means as a quantizer control at the project's sizes; relQE; EV only under Euclid
ideas.risk: k-means with 144 centroids on 600 items degenerates toward 1-NN and G explodes for every map: cap K at N/5 or report G only where the quantiser has >= 5 items per centroid; PAM is a weaker ceiling than DBA k-means under DTW, so G_DTW flatters maps a little.
ideas.expected_gain: moderate for cross-size reading and for comparing PD with the other sets; none on same-size verdicts (by design)
ideas.problems: G >= 1 is not guaranteed under DTW with PAM as the floor: a DTW-SOM prototype is an average (warped update), and averages beat medoids on mean DTW (that is DBA's whole point), so G_DTW < 1 is possible and would be misread as 'the map fits better than a quantiser'. The project already has the right DTW floor for free: its batch DTW-SOM is DBA, so DBA k-means is the batch DTW-SOM with the neighbourhood set to zero. 'G flat in K for the plain SOM' is a prediction, not a known property: with the final radius 0.5 neighbours still get ~13% of the pull, and whether that price shrinks with K is exactly what the experiment would find, so the win criterion should not be framed as a pass/fail for the measure. k-means at K = 144 on 600 items degenerates toward 1-NN, as admitted. Kaufman & Rousseeuw (1990, Finding Groups in Data) is the PAM reference.
ideas.corrections: Use DBA k-means (batch DTW-SOM, radius 0, same seed and start) as the DTW floor and R's kmeans with the same random start under Euclid; cap K at N/5 or report G only where the quantiser has >= 5 items per centroid; report G and EV_DTW as unitless columns over the size series and the 'price of order' curve G vs K per variant. State that G can fall below 1 when a medoid floor is used. This supersedes L1's fit-null.

ideas.title: Integer SOM for the field: Manhattan/SAD on int8-int16 data with int32 accumulators and an exact integer DTW
ideas.what_it_changes: A fixed-point scalar type plugged into the existing template (train_T<Q>): integer local cost |x - m| or (x - m)^2, int32/int64 accumulators, prototypes kept in a 32-bit word (Q8.24, or int16 with a residual accumulator) so that late updates are not swamped; on the device, mapping uses the integer SAD (sum of absolute differences, one instruction per 8-16 values on Cortex-M DSP and x86 psadbw) and an integer DP that stores 2-bit direction codes for the backtrace (4 KB for L = 125 instead of the 126 KB double table). The user named Manhattan: this is where it earns its keep.
ideas.mechanism: Integer addition is exact and associative, so the DP and the distance sums have no accumulation error at all and are bit-identical on any hardware and in any order; the only precision loss is the quantisation of the inputs, which the data tolerate (measured: asinh-scaled PD at 8 bits gives the same QE/TE/purity/ARI as fp64 over 5 seeds; 6 bits slight; 4 bits QE +1.3%). Manhattan needs no multiply and its sums fit int16 for L = 125 at 8 bits (max 31,875); squared local costs with 8-bit inputs fit int32 along a path of 250 cells. The benchmark's own finding that mapping with DTW captures much of DTW's gain means a DTW-trained map can be deployed with integer DTW mapping only.
ideas.why_pd: The field sensor is a microcontroller or FPGA; budget on a 100 MHz Cortex-M4: 100 units x 125 points of SAD about 0.3 ms per pulse; integer DTW with a 10% band about 0.3 M cell operations, 10-30 ms per pulse, fine for tens of pulses per second, not for kHz pulse rates, hence LB_Keogh pruning (exact in integers) and DTW only among the top few Euclidean candidates. Loudness is already companded by asinh (P8), so 8 bits suffice.
ideas.why_movement: Wearables: 12-16 bit IMU ADC, CMSIS-DSP int16 SAD, 3-6 channels; the multichannel dependent DTW multiplies the local-cost work by the number of channels.
ideas.control: Two controls, seed by seed: the fp64 Manhattan SOM for the integer pointwise map, and the fp64 DTW-SOM for the integer DTW; plus post-training quantisation (train in fp64, round prototypes to the device word, map with integer distances) against quantisation-aware integer training.
ideas.how_to_test: pd_acoustic, gestures (3 channels), GunPoint; sizes 5 x 5, 7 x 7, 10 x 10; seeds 1-10; input bits 16, 12, 8 (and 6 to find the floor); read QE/EV/TE/KL/TP/purity/ARI/NMI/used judged in fp64 on the unquantised data, winner agreement with the fp64 map, exact-tie count, bytes of RAM and operations per waveform. Win: purity and ARI within the seed spread and QE within 2% of fp64 at 8 bits; a QE stall at low bits diagnoses swamping (then widen the prototype word or add stochastic rounding) rather than winner error.
ideas.cost: One to two days of C++ for the type and the direction-code DP; runtime at or below fp64 on the PC; MCU figures above.
anchors: Gupta, Agrawal, Gopalakrishnan & Narayanan (2015) Deep learning with limited numerical precision (stochastic rounding)
ITU-T G.711 (mu-law / A-law companding)
Keogh & Ratanamahatana (2005) Exact indexing of dynamic time warping (LB_Keogh, already used by the project)
CMSIS-NN / CMSIS-DSP int8 and int16 kernels, Lai, Suda & Chandra (2018) (unverified details)
ideas.already_tested: no for integer arithmetic; the bit depth of the data was measured in this session (8-bit asinh lossless, 5 seeds, Euclid, synthetic PD); the Manhattan fp64 variant is coded in ns_maps.R but has no benchmark results yet.
ideas.risk: Update swamping in a narrow prototype word (27.7% of last-pass coordinate updates fall below half an ulp in fp16; int16 has the same problem) freezes the fine phase; a rounded LB bound in floats can prune the true winner (exact in integers, or add slack); Manhattan's winner differs from the Euclidean one, so compare only within one distance as the project insists.
ideas.expected_gain: None on quality (the aim is equality with fp64 at a fraction of the cost and with bit-identical results on every machine); large on deployability; the measures that must be read are winner agreement and purity/ARI, not QE alone.
ideas.problems: (1) Stale on Manhattan: the full bench cache (5 seeds, sizes 5/7/10/14) already holds it. On the PD stand-in ARI beats the online SOM on 5/5 seeds at 7, 10 and 14 (0.187 vs 0.131 at 7 x 7, purity 0.866 vs 0.833), QE judged in L2 is worse 0/5 (a different contest, as expected), TE worse on 3/5; no consistent gain on CBF or gestures (Section 6's box: 'a different contest, not a better one'). (2) The 2-bit direction-code table is a red herring for the field unit: mapping needs the DTW distance only, never the path, and a distance-only DP needs two rows (about 1 KB in int32 for L = 125); the backtrace matters only for on-device training. (3) Two experiments are bundled: post-training quantisation with integer mapping (cheap, and it is roadmap item 5 of the next-steps report made concrete) and quantisation-aware integer training (needed only if the device adapts); the win criterion mixes them. (4) The 8-bit sufficiency figure comes from the synthetic stand-in, whose asinh values are continuous (make_pd adds 0.2 mPa of noise before asinh), Euclid only, 5 seeds; the real recordings carry ADC steps, so the floor may sit one or two bits higher. (5) MCU timings are back-of-envelope and unverified. The integer mechanism itself is sound: SAD and the DP are exact and order-independent, L1 sums fit int16 at 8 bits (31,875), squared costs fit int32, and LB_Keogh is indeed in the project (benchmark Section 2).
ideas.corrections: Run part (a) first and alone: train in fp64, round prototypes and inputs to b in {16, 12, 8, 6} bits, map with integer SAD, integer squared-Euclid and distance-only integer DTW (10% band), on pd_acoustic and the gestures, 5 x 5 / 7 x 7 / 10 x 10, seeds 1-10; read winner agreement with the fp64 map, per-class purity, ARI, the detection AUROC of Section 7 and the share of exact ties; judge each device map against the fp64 map of the SAME distance (L1 against L1, L2 against L2, DTW against DTW), never across. Part (b), integer training with a Q8.24 word and a swamped-update counter, only if the device must adapt. Add fp16 storage as one rung of the same ladder (that absorbs P7). Confirm the Manhattan-finds-PD-classes result on the real data, judged with its own distance, before choosing L1 as the device distance.

ideas.title: asinh as the companding law: how many bits each PD class keeps, and where the knee should sit
ideas.what_it_changes: A data-side experiment with the fp64 core: quantise asinh(p / p0) uniformly to b bits before training (16, 12, 10, 8, 6, 4) against quantising the raw pressure linearly to the same b bits and then applying asinh; vary the knee p0 in {0.1, 1, 10 mPa, the noise RMS}; report per-class purity and per-class QE, distinct values per series, and the detection AUROC of the distance to the winner that ns_quality.R already computes.
ideas.mechanism: asinh is mu-law: constant relative resolution above the knee, so 8 bits cover four decades at about 8% amplitude steps, whereas linear quantisation spends its bits on the loudest class and zeroes the quiet ones. Measured here (synthetic PD, Euclid, 5 seeds, 7 x 7): asinh at 8 bits equals fp64 on QE/TE/purity/ARI (48 distinct values per series); 6 bits TE 0.148 vs 0.165 and purity 0.790 vs 0.806; 4 bits QE +1.3%; raw linear 12 bits QE +0.8% with only 26 distinct values (the quiet classes are flat); raw linear 8 bits collapses (QE 22.3 vs 12.2, purity 0.63 vs 0.81). Rounding the data to an fp16 significand changes nothing. The knee decides which classes live in the linear region and keep waveform shape (noise, void) and which keep only log-amplitude and ringing shape; the precision budget per class is bits x (class range / total range).
ideas.why_pd: A field unit stores or transmits 8-bit samples and has a 12-bit ADC; this says the asinh scale makes 8 bits enough and that the knee is a design parameter of the classifier, not a cosmetic choice; the per-class purity of noise and void is the number to watch.
ideas.why_movement: Accelerometers at +-16 g with 0.01 g tremor pose the same question per channel; a per-channel asinh knee at the sensor noise is the same companding argument.
ideas.control: fp64 unquantised asinh with the project's knee of 1 mPa, same seed; for QE compare only within one knee because the knee changes the metric.
ideas.how_to_test: Real pd_acoustic, seeds 1-10, sizes 5 x 5, 7 x 7, 10 x 10, Euclid and DTW, 20 passes; read per-class purity, QE/EV/TE/KL/TP/ARI/NMI/used, detection AUROC per class, distinct values per series. Win for bits: the smallest b whose measures stay within the seed spread of fp64 (expected 8 on asinh, 12 or more on raw); win for the knee: a knee that raises noise and void purity on at least 7 of 10 seeds without lowering corona and air-gap purity.
ideas.cost: Trivial; the fp64 core; minutes.
anchors: ITU-T G.711 Pulse code modulation of voice frequencies (mu-law and A-law companding)
Parks, Roederer & Moore (2006) arcsinh display transform for flow cytometry (unverified details)
Project: benchmark pd_acoustic description, 'pressure as asinh(p / 1 mPa)'
ideas.already_tested: partly: bits measured in this session on the synthetic PD stand-in (Euclid only); the knee was never varied in the project; real pd_acoustic and DTW not run.
ideas.risk: The synthetic set has continuous asinh values while the real recordings already carry ADC steps, so the real floor may be one or two bits higher; a knee below the noise floor turns noise waveforms into log-scaled hash and may lower their purity; the knee changes the distances, so QE across knees is not comparable.
ideas.expected_gain: Large at 8 bits relative to linear quantisation (collapse vs equality); none at fp32/fp64; the knee may improve the separation of the quiet classes, unknown until run on the real data.
ideas.problems: Two experiments under one title. The bit-depth half belongs to the deployment ladder (P6) and was measured by the proposer on the synthetic stand-in only, whose asinh values are continuous (make_pd adds 0.2 mPa of noise before asinh), Euclid only, 5 seeds; the real recordings already carry ADC steps, so the 8-bit floor is a guess until run on them. The movement claim is decorative: gestures span about two decades, not four, and the usual question there is per-channel z-normalisation, not companding. The knee half is the real idea and is untested in the project (the benchmark fixes 1 mPa everywhere), with a sound mechanism: the knee sets the amplitude where the metric switches from linear (waveform shape kept) to logarithmic (log-amplitude plus ringing shape), i.e. which classes keep their waveform, and the noise RMS is the data-driven choice in the project's own style. Two traps the test must respect: purity rises with units (compare at one size) and QE across knees is a different metric (the idea says so). Parks, Roederer & Moore (2006) is the Logicle paper, of which arcsinh is the special case; the attribution is loose but not wrong.
ideas.corrections: Make the knee the experiment: p0 in {noise RMS, 0.3, 1, 3, 10 mPa} on the real pd_acoustic, Euclid and DTW, 7 x 7 and 10 x 10, seeds 1-10; read per-class purity and ARI at a fixed size, the detection AUROC per class, and KL/TE within one knee. Add a second control that Section 7 of the next-steps report motivates: an amplitude-blind distance (cosine or SBD) with asinh(peak) appended as a weighted 126th value, because if the knee helps only by deciding how much loudness enters the Euclidean distance, that is the cleaner version of the same knob. Move the bit-depth rungs into P6. Before any claim about plateaus or bits, report the ADC depth of the recordings and the share of samples at full scale.

dropped.title: Fracture mechanics for tearing: cut a link when its stored strain energy exceeds a Griffith threshold, let cracks propagate, heal with hysteresis
dropped.lens: continuum mechanics: Griffith energy criterion, crack propagation
dropped.why_dropped: The 'not tested' list is partly wrong and the mechanism adds knobs. (a) 'Enabled when the radius falls below 1.5 rather than at a fixed fraction of training' is the same thing: the project's schedule_plain is a linear ramp, so radius < 1.5 is a fixed fraction of the steps, and tearing that starts at 10-75% was tested and 'removed the effect' while stopping the shredding. (b) The 'absolute' threshold is not absolute: U_rs sums h(r,s) d^2 over the items a unit wins in a pass, so it scales with the unit's hit count and with h, which has fallen to about exp(-2) per lattice step by the time the radius is 0.5; late in training every U_rs is small and G_c has to be rescaled to the schedule, which is a relative rule again, plus kappa and the hysteresis factor: three knobs where the median rule had one. (c) The energy 'released by cutting a link' is not the pairwise cross term once the pull follows graph distance: cutting (r,s) changes h for every pair whose shortest path used the link, so the Griffith reading is a metaphor after all. (d) The tearing summary's own finding kills the application claim: 'clustering the prototypes finds the same clusters with any map', so pieces = classes adds nothing to the Ward cut for PD, and on a 5x5 gesture map with 6-10 classes pieces cannot equal classes. (e) The prior is 0 wins in 216 set-size-threshold comparisons, rejoin and mend no gain; the proposer's own expected gain is 'small' and the stated value is a 'clean final verdict', which the project already has.

dropped.title: Elastic net: the lattice as real springs, with DTW springs that share timing between neighbouring prototypes
dropped.lens: energy with tension (Durbin & Willshaw), elastic maps (Gorban & Zinovyev)
dropped.why_dropped: Not tested as such, but the Euclidean arm is a reparametrisation of two measured things: a soft data term (L1's soft arm; the batch SOM is its K -> 0 limit: best QE, worst TE) and a spring that pulls prototypes toward their lattice neighbours in data space, which is what a non-zero final radius does (metrics report 4b: final radius 1 lowers TE and raises QE, KL minimum near 1). So the sheet arm is a final-radius sweep with extra lines. The only new ingredient, the DTW spring, rests on a doubtful mechanism: TE asks whether an item's two nearest prototypes are lattice neighbours; two neighbouring prototypes whose events are offset in time are still close under DTW within the band, so timing disagreement does not break TE unless it exceeds the band; re-timing raised TE because moving points in time changed every item-prototype distance, not because neighbours disagreed. The deliverable for gestures ('prototypes that morph into one another') is readability, not ARI; the TSP arm is off the user's stated targets; and the loss of LB_Keogh doubles the DTW-SOM's cost, which is already 3-15x the classic map's. The proposer's expected gain on ARI is 'unknown' and the growing DTW-SOM already keeps timing without springs.

dropped.title: Replica exchange across seeds: swap maps between temperatures instead of restarting
dropped.lens: Monte Carlo: parallel tempering (Swendsen & Wang; Hukushima & Nemoto)
dropped.why_dropped: (a) The 'exact within L1's picture' claim is wrong: the replicas are deterministic-annealing or stochastic-approximation descents on prototypes, not MCMC samplers of exp(-beta E), so the Metropolis swap preserves no distribution and 'detailed balance' does not apply; what remains is a heuristic 'swap maps when the colder one has the higher energy'. (b) Every replica also runs the radius schedule, so all are cold at the end whatever beta says, late swaps are moot and early swaps exchange near-random maps, as the proposer admits. (c) The product, 'the coldest replica', is one map picked by energy; that is the project's best-of-R by KL, and the proposed control will show the swaps add nothing beyond it; for gesture maps 'picks among near-equivalent orderings by energy' is best-of-R under another name. (d) It discards the researcher's method: collapsing 10 seeds into one delivered map removes the seed-by-seed comparison (10 seed groups per setting, no within-group pairing). (e) Nothing is specific to PD or movement; the PD claim ('escape folds without widening the radius') is the CHAOSOM trade the project has already measured twice. Depends entirely on L1 being run first.

dropped.title: Graph heat kernel as the neighbourhood function on grown, torn and rejoined maps
dropped.lens: diffusion / heat equation on graphs (Kondor & Lafferty)
dropped.why_dropped: Mechanism is sound (diffusion kernel counts paths) but its scope in this project is close to empty. (a) On the plain lattice it is the Gaussian up to boundary terms, and the growing map grows to the usual full lattice, so the kernel differs from the geodesic Gaussian only during growth (7 to K units) and at the ragged border. (b) The normalisation H_t(c,s)/H_t(c,c) does not remove the border effect: a border unit's heat has nowhere to leave, so its neighbourhood is wider than an interior unit's under the Gaussian; that changes exactly the border behaviour TP reacts to and confounds the comparison the proposer wants to make. (c) The torn maps where a graded rejoin would matter lost to a smaller start radius on pull strength, not coupling shape, and rejoin at 40% gave the plain SOM to the last bit: the early map forgets everything, graded or not. (d) Nothing PD- or gesture-specific; the proposer's own expected gain is 'small, on TE/KL of grown and rejoined maps only', and the rejoined maps are a closed file.

dropped.title: Conservation of momentum: heavy-ball prototype updates, tested against Polyak iterate averaging
dropped.lens: dynamical systems / optimisation (Polyak's heavy ball, Ruppert-Polyak averaging)
dropped.why_dropped: Not tested, cheap, and almost certainly a wash as written. (a) Momentum with constant mu is a learning rate alpha/(1 - mu); the proposer's own effective-rate control makes the momentum arm a wash by construction, and in the ordering phase it can twist the map. (b) Averaging over the last pass at alpha = 0.01: a unit sees about N/K items per pass, each moving it by at most 1% of a step, so the delivered prototype differs in the third decimal, as the proposer admits. (c) The seed-to-seed spread of ARI is decided in the ordering phase (which arrangement the map falls into), not by the last items seen, so 'seed spread halved' cannot happen by averaging the end; the reproducibility claim for PD and gesture maps is decorative. (d) The only arm with a real mechanism, Ruppert-Polyak's larger step plus averaging (end alpha at 0.1 rather than 0.01, average the last two passes), is not in the proposal and its controls (plain ending at 0.1, plain ending at 0.01, batch SOM) are not either; the proposed 'one extra pass' control does not cover it.

dropped.title: Phase-oscillator SOM: Kuramoto's coupling as the exact update for circular channels (PRPD phase, joint angles)
dropped.lens: dynamical systems: Kuramoto model, von Mises statistics
dropped.why_dropped: Untestable on the project's data for both targets. pd_acoustic is triggered on the current pulse and records no AC phase (the proposer says so); both gesture sets, GesturePebbleZ1 and ShakeGestureWiimoteZ, are single-axis Z accelerometer series with no heading, wrist-rotation or joint-angle channel, and several channels are themselves on the never-tested list. So this is a data-acquisition proposal, not a SOM improvement the researcher can run. Mechanism: the Kuramoto identification is loose in the same way as the elastic-net spring: the neighbour's pull is toward the item's phase, sin(phi - theta_s), not toward the winner's theta_c; there is no sin(theta_c - theta_s) term in the update, so 'phases synchronise locally' is a by-product of sharing items, as in any SOM. The (cos, sin) flat control is strong: no seam, prototypes renormalised to the circle post hoc, and the von Mises step differs from it only in step length, so the ARI difference is likely nil. In gesture practice heading and device orientation are removed (rotation-invariant features) because users do not face the same way, rather than modelled as a map axis; circular joint angles belong to mocap data, not to the wrist-IMU sets here. PRPD phase is indeed the standard PD discriminator (correct from memory), but its standard use is a phase-amplitude histogram, and a phase-tagged recording would make the (cos, sin)-appended DTW-SOM the first test, with the cylinder lattice a later refinement.

dropped.title: The exponent of the local cost: Minkowski-p sweep from L1 to Chebyshev
dropped.lens: distances and alignments inside the SOM
dropped.why_dropped: The only plausible range (1 <= p < 2) is L1's Huber sweep, which the author admits ('the continuation of idea 1'). The rest (p > 2, Chebyshev with a log-sum-exp temperature tau) is a knob without a reason: the gradient |r|^(p-1) explodes for p > 2 and needs the 'typical residual^(p-2)' rescaling, a free parameter that can manufacture a gain - the chaos/tearing pattern the project already learned to distrust. The author expects harm at p -> inf and a wash near 2, QE is not comparable across p so the headline fit measure disappears, and pow() per DTW cell costs 2-3x for a predicted null. For PD a pulse judged by its single worst-matched sample is judged by trigger jitter.

dropped.title: Mahalanobis / whitened distance: count every direction once
dropped.lens: distances and alignments inside the SOM
dropped.why_dropped: (1) The 'rotation only' PCA control is vacuous: the Euclidean SOM is invariant to an orthogonal rotation (winner choice and update commute with it), so a full-rank PCA rotation reproduces the raw control up to rounding; only truncation or rescaling changes anything. (2) Whitening by the TOTAL covariance shrinks exactly the directions along which the classes differ most, because with four well-separated classes those are the largest-variance directions; the Mahalanobis argument holds for the WITHIN-class covariance, which needs labels. Unsupervised whitening before clustering is a known way to lose cluster separation. (3) 'Near-Toeplitz, eigenvectors near-sinusoids' is false for trigger-aligned pulses: they are non-stationary inside the 250 us window (onset, ringing, decay at fixed positions), so whitening is not a spectral equaliser. (4) A 125 x 125 covariance from 600 series has small eigenvalues that are estimation noise, and W amplifies precisely those; eps and k are knobs. (5) The per-unit diagonal metric estimates 125 variances from about 6 series per unit on a 100-unit map.

dropped.title: Exact lower-bound pruning inside the training loop
dropped.lens: distances and alignments inside the SOM
dropped.why_dropped: By construction it changes no quality measure, so it is plumbing, not a brainstorm idea, and the user asked how to improve classification. The project already found that 11-15% fewer alignments bought a tenth of the time; the update alignments (every unit within the radius, every step) cannot be pruned, so the saving sits in the late-training winner search only - the author's own 20-40% headline - and with the widening window and the growing map the early passes are already cheap. Exactness trap: with ties (prototypes started as copies of items, births as copies), ordering units by bound and early-abandoning can return a different tied winner than the index-order loop, so 'bit for bit' needs the same tie rule (lowest index among exact ties, abandon only on strict greater-than). The envelope refresh must be O(L) with Lemire's deque, not O(L*w), or it costs as much as the alignment it saves.
