dropped.title: Change what makes the growing map give birth: by hits (conscience) or by novelty (grow-when-required), not by error
dropped.why_dropped: (1) Partly tested: the growing DTW-SOM already gives birth from the unit where the map fits worst (error-driven parent), at even steps; the drafts also tried integrate-and-fire births (absolute and relative error thresholds), births at chaotic and at random steps, and all were within seed noise of births at even steps (summary Section 7, draft table). Arm (b), a novelty threshold on one item's distance, is the integrate-and-fire rule with a shorter memory plus a habituation counter: a new knob next to a tested one that gained nothing. (2) The mechanism rests on an assertion ('error-driven births starve the noise class') that can be checked for free on the cached growing maps (units per class) and was not. (3) 'The noise model needs the most resolution to lower FAR' is doubtful: in asinh units the noise class is compact; FAR depends on where the threshold sits, not on how many units model noise; one well-thresholded unit may do. (4) The threshold 'from the data (noise RMS in pascals)' is not on the scale of the DTW distance between asinh series, so it would still be set by hand; that is the tearing lesson (low thresholds shred the map) in a new place. (5) The experiment cannot be read until PD6/PD8 provide FAR and held-out recall, so it is third in line, and the growing map's own benchmark result was 'did not find the classes better', which lowers the prior that a birth rule will.

dropped.title: If the record carries the mains phase: add (cos phi, sin phi) as two channels and read a PRPD pattern per unit
dropped.why_dropped: (1) Untestable as far as the project's reports go: the pd_acoustic series are 125 samples with no phase or time stamp, and nothing in the five reports or the data description mentions the test voltage type or phase; the Zenodo record could not be checked from this session (network blocked), so the idea is conditional on metadata nobody has seen. (2) Even with phase, the design has a known inflation problem the proposal itself admits: one source per class in a lab means phase is nearly deterministic per class, so ARI gains would measure the lab set-up, not the map. (3) Sample size: 150 pulses per class spread over 25-100 units gives 1-20 pulses per unit, far too few for a per-unit phase histogram to be a readable PRPD pattern (PRPD patterns rest on thousands of pulses over many cycles). (4) Two columns of weight lambda against 125 waveform samples carry about 2 lambda^2 / (125 var) of the squared distance; for the channel to matter lambda must be large, at which point the map sorts by phase and the waveform is decoration: a knob whose useful setting is the degenerate one. (5) The movement analogue (gait phase as a context channel) is decorative.

dropped.title: Soft-DTW prototypes against cycle-skipping on ringing pulses
dropped.why_dropped: (1) Soft-DTW is not a distance: softdtw(x, x) is not 0 and the value can be negative, and it is biased by how many low-cost paths a pair admits (smoother series get lower values); used for the winner choice it would prefer units for reasons unrelated to fit. The proposal uses it for the winner and the update without saying so. (2) gamma is a new knob in squared data units; it must scale with the asinh range and the three values are a sweep, which is the chaos/tearing pattern (a knob before a mechanism is shown to be needed). (3) The claimed failure (cycle skipping blurring prototypes) has not been shown on this data: the reports give a 'bunched prototype timing' on CBF, not a spectral-peak drift on PD, and the dominant frequency per class is unknown (PD4's diagnostic). PD5's 2-3 % window is a one-line control that removes the possibility of a one-cycle skip; if it fixes the prototypes there is nothing left for soft-DTW, as the proposal's own risk line concedes. (4) The project found DTW's PD gain mostly in the reading step and already fixed prototype timing twice (births from data, widening window); the expected ARI gain is 'small' by the author's own estimate at 2-3x the cost. Mechanism is real (Cuturi & Blondel 2017 ICML; cycle skipping is a genuine FWI problem, Virieux & Operto 2009, Geophysics 74(6)), but a seed-by-seed run is not worth the time before PD5 shows the symptom.

dropped.title: Tear and rejoin by data support: GNG edge ageing on the hex lattice
dropped.why_dropped: Three objections, any one of which sinks it as written. (1) Scale of a_max: GNG ages an edge per WIN of the unit, and the project's maps have K ~ 5*sqrt(N) units, i.e. N/K ~ 6 wins per unit per pass on pd_acoustic (1.5 on a 20x20). With six lattice links and the runner-up spread over them, a link's refresh interval has mean ~6 wins, so a_max = N/K kills about a third of healthy in-cluster links per pass by chance ((5/6)^6 = 0.33); the whole grid {N/K, 2N/K, 5N/K} sits in the noise regime. GNG works because it has many items per node; this project does not. (2) Timing: the idea starts ageing only once the radius is below 1, i.e. at the project's 0.5 floor, where the Gaussian pull on a direct neighbour is exp(-2) = 0.135 and on a 2-step unit 3e-4. Cutting a link then removes almost nothing, so either it starts earlier (and repeats the 1%-shredding of threshold 2.5) or it barely changes the prototypes, in which case the 'pieces' are a graph read on top of an ordinary map, which L10 gives from the cached maps at zero training cost. (3) Mechanism conflict: a link dies exactly where winner and runner-up are NOT lattice neighbours, i.e. at folds, and removing the pull at a fold locks it in. The project's one winning ingredient, the floating radius (Der et al.), does the opposite: it widens the pull at folds and that gave the order back (TE 0.076 -> 0.060). Running ageing inside the growing map puts the two rules in direct opposition. The PD claim (units stranded between a 'noise ball' and corona, counted dead) appears in no report; it is an inference. Reproducibility: ages at exactly a_max and rebirth make the link set flicker; the piece count becomes order-dependent noise unless deaths/rebirths per link are logged.

dropped.title: DTW neural gas: rank-based update of every unit along its own warping path, no lattice
dropped.why_dropped: The outcome is largely known before the run: neural gas sits between the SOM and k-means on QE by construction, the project already found that Ward on the prototypes finds the same clusters with any map (so ARI will not move), and TE/KL/TP are undefined, so nothing the project values is tested. It is not an improvement of the classical SOM but a replacement of the lattice, and the user asked to improve the map. The CHL graph as a cluster count inherits L1's few-items-per-unit noise (N/K ~ 6 on PD), only read rather than trained. Cost claim is optimistic: the growing loop skips units by LB_Keogh / small pull, while NG must align and backtrack all K units every step, so it forfeits that pruning. Reproducibility (my lens): a rank-based update needs a sort of K DTW distances per step, and the benchmark explicitly tests integer series full of ties; without a stable sort with an index tie-break the ranks, and hence the maps, differ between R's order() and std::sort, breaking the project's last-bit reproducibility standard. Storing K cost matrices (100 x 125 x 25 doubles ~ 2.5 MB) is fine.

dropped.title: Conscience (DeSieno) against dead units: the principled version of what the chaotic units did by accident
dropped.why_dropped: The question it wants to close is already closed: the chaotic-units report ran the bounded control ('long-run mean output, no chaos'), which rescued dead units as well as the chaos did (200 of 200 starts) and gained nothing where no unit was dead. A conscience bias is a third way to rescue dead units; it can only repeat that finding. DeSieno's conscience was designed for competitive learning without a neighbourhood; the SOM's wide-radius phase already recruits every unit, and the idea switches the bias on only below radius 1, when the remaining dead units are the ones left in gaps between clusters (the blobs: 11.8-16.7 of 64). Equiprobable quantization then drags a gap unit onto a cluster edge while its lattice neighbours stay on the other side: a fold, the exact risk the idea names, with TE up. The PD claim (idle units between a 'noise ball' and the loud classes) is in no report. Precision of the frequency estimate: with B = 1e-4 the time constant is 10,000 steps, about 17 passes on N = 600, so p_i never settles within a 20-pass run and the bias is dominated by the start value; with N/K ~ 6 wins per pass per unit the estimate is noisy at any B. Two knobs (B, C) for a rule the project's own lesson 4 says tends to buy order for fit.

dropped.title: Toroidal (and spherical) lattice: no rim, and a home for cyclic variables such as mains phase
dropped.why_dropped: The anchor to the project is misread: the metrics report's rim 'dent' passage says the error there is harmless and 'the map is fine here; the point just lies beyond its edge'; it is not evidence that rim units are where dead units or errors pile up. Mechanism for non-cyclic data is backwards: a torus has no boundary, so wrapped around a bounded data sheet it must bring its seam rows back over data already covered; lattice neighbours across the seam are far apart in data space, which raises KL, TP and full-lattice TE. The predicted 'small gain on dead units and KL for non-cyclic data' has no mechanism; the known result is a loss. Every data set in the project is non-cyclic at the item level: pd_acoustic is trigger-aligned with no phase, and Italy Power Demand's items are days, not phases of one cycle. The genuinely cyclic cases (PRPD phase, gait stride phase) are not in the project, so the proposed test on existing data answers only the rim question. For one cyclic variable the right lattice is a cylinder (ring x line), not a torus, and the idea's own fair control, a planar map with sin/cos of phase appended, already carries the same information and will be hard to beat. Venue correction: Ito, Miyoshi & Masuyama (2000) is the 16th Fuzzy System Symposium (Japan Society for Fuzzy Theory), not IIZUKA 2000; Kiso (2012) is Kiso & Seki, confirmed.

dropped.title: Bagged SOMs with lattice alignment, and bumping (keep the best of B by KL)
dropped.why_dropped: The lattice-alignment step is mis-specified: the project's lattice is a rectangular hex grid with offset rows, whose symmetry group is at most the rectangle's 4 operations (and with an odd number of rows some reflections do not map the grid onto itself), not 12; the 12 belong to a hexagon-shaped lattice. Alignment then falls to a pairwise-swap quadratic assignment, a heuristic whose result depends on the sweep order. Fusing aligned prototypes by averaging smooths them, so TE falls and QE rises for a trivial reason (the idea admits this); the medoid-per-cell fallback avoids the blur but builds a patchwork whose neighbours were trained in different maps, the re-timing inconsistency (TE up). The target, lower seed-to-seed SD, is not a better map under the project's rule (seed-by-seed wins at matched size); most of the SD the project sees is lattice orientation, which alignment removes before any bagging happens. B = 5 maps cost 5x and the fair rival, one map trained 5x longer, has the project's own evidence on its side (5 vs 20 passes: TE 0.104 vs 0.064). Petrakieva & Fyfe (2003) confirmed. Bumping is zero-cost on the cached 10 seeds and is a legitimate selection (KL is label-free, so reporting the KL-best map's ARI is not a leak), and the idea itself expects bumping to capture most of the gain.

dropped.title: Jigsaw: re-seat torn pieces (or any map's units) on the lattice by swaps that shorten the seams
dropped.why_dropped: Part (a) rests on a hypothesis the reports do not support: the tear-and-join report says 'rejoined late, the disorder stays', not that pieces drifted from their cells. At threshold 2.5 the map is in dozens of pieces by 1% of training, and pieces must tile the lattice, so 'slide a whole piece by a symmetry plus a translation' is impossible without moving the others; only unit swaps remain, and a quadratic assignment by wire length has no reason to recreate the pull the half-radius SOM applied evenly for the whole schedule (lesson 5). The idea itself expects (a) to lose. Part (b) is a post-hoc optimisation of the order measures: minimising the U-matrix total is not minimising TE (which counts item winner/runner-up adjacency), so swaps can lower wire length and raise TE; and if TE/KL are optimised directly from the cached N x K table it is explicitly optimising the measure. After re-seating, each prototype is still the smoothed mean of its OLD neighbourhood, so the map is no longer self-consistent (the re-timing objection). Reproducibility: 2-opt outcomes depend on the candidate-pair order; it must be fixed and stated. Croes (1958) is the right 2-opt citation. Nothing here touches PD or movement data specifically.

dropped.title: Rigid-body alignment before DTW: one rotation per (item, prototype) pair, the 3-D cousin of SBD's shift
dropped.lens: movement / gesture / HAR from wearable sensors
dropped.why_dropped: A rotation fitted per (item, prototype) PAIR breaks the SOM's ordering mechanism: the winner's lattice neighbours are each pulled towards a differently rotated copy of the item, whereas topological order comes from neighbours being pulled towards the same point. Nothing in 'prototypes live in a canonical frame by consensus' enforces a consensus; adjacent units can settle in different frames, the map becomes unreadable, and the Ward cut on prototypes (how ARI is read) then needs rotation-DTW too, which the idea does not say. With gravity in the signal the Kabsch fit is dominated by aligning the mean vectors, leaving yaw weakly determined for mild gestures: the degenerate-SVD case the idea fears is the common case, not the early-training exception. The analogy to SBD's lag is loose: one lag found by cross-correlation versus three parameters inside an alternating DTW/Kabsch loop (an ICP). Moderate C++ work and 2x alignments for a nuisance whose size on the researcher's real data is unknown; at 0 degrees it is a wash by the proposer's own account.

dropped.title: Learned channel weights inside the SOM (diagonal metric adaptation)
dropped.lens: movement / gesture / HAR from wearable sensors
dropped.why_dropped: The mechanism is circular. The units were split along the channels that already carried high weight, so between-unit variance is high and within-unit variance low exactly on the channels in use: the ratio rewards whatever the map already does. A quiet but informative channel (on which the map did not split) gets a low ratio and is down-weighted further; a loud, structured nuisance (gravity offset, orientation) gets a high ratio and is up-weighted. The floor and once-per-pass update slow this, they do not remove it. The proposed test is weak: a white-noise channel's prototypes converge to about zero, so its contribution to the distance is nearly the same for every unit and barely moves the winner, hence both the control and the variant will be a wash on the noise channels, and the x10 channel is fixed by the plain control (global per-channel z-scaling) alone. Hammer & Villmann's GRLVQ and Kaski et al.'s learning metrics both use labels (auxiliary data); neither supports an unsupervised Fisher ratio over units, which the idea itself calls a heuristic with no reference.

dropped.title: Time-warp (and rotation) augmentation of each presentation: the cheap Euclidean route to speed invariance
dropped.lens: movement / gesture / HAR from wearable sensors
dropped.why_dropped: A Euclidean prototype under random warps converges to the mean over the warp family, which is a BLURRED template: exactly the 'smeared ramp' the project identified as the Kohonen SOM's failure on CBF, now made deliberate. No invariance is learned, because a mean cannot encode one (a CNN can, which is why the cited augmentation papers work). The winner choice on original items against blurred prototypes is Gaussian-smoothed Euclidean matching, and the idea omits the plain control that does the same job deterministically at zero cost: the Euclidean SOM on Gaussian-smoothed items or prototypes. On CBF-like data the Ward cut on blurrier prototypes should merge classes, so ARI is expected to fall, which the proposer half admits. The PD claim is empty: the pulses are trigger-aligned and the 10% band (12 samples) already covers +/-2 samples of jitter. This repeats the pattern the project warned about: a stochastic knob (sigma) standing in for a reason.

dropped.title: A DTW band learned per unit (R-K bands): no window sweep
dropped.lens: movement / gesture / HAR from wearable sensors
dropped.why_dropped: Two structural flaws, not tuning matters. (1) DTW cost is non-increasing in the band, so units with different bands compete on incomparable costs: a wide-band unit under-reports every distance, wins more, sees more wandering paths and widens again. The cap, the 90% envelope and the delayed start only slow the loop the idea already fears. (2) The envelope of paths computed under band w can never exceed w, so the data can only SHRINK a band; widening comes only from the fixed margin. 'The band is learned from the data' is therefore false for the widening direction, which is the direction CBF needed (10% to 20%). The reference is misapplied: R-K bands are learned per CLASS with labels by a search that maximises accuracy, which is what makes the band-dependent costs comparable there; the unsupervised per-unit envelope has no such correction. The payoff is bounded by the best fixed band, and the sweep it replaces costs the project 3 seeds x 5 widths. Not already tested: 'a window per unit' is on the never-tested list, correct.

dropped.title: Two-level map for continuous streams: a frame-SOM trajectory cuts the stream, a DTW-SOM on trajectories names the gestures
dropped.lens: movement / gesture / HAR from wearable sensors
dropped.why_dropped: Level 2 on winner coordinates is unsound: lattice coordinates are not a metric of the data (folds put very different frames on adjacent units and similar frames on distant ones), so DTW with a Euclidean local cost on a 2-channel coordinate series measures lattice geometry, not motion. The dwell detector uses the same information as the energy threshold (frames of raw axes plus |a|), so the only mechanism by which it can beat the threshold is a slow orientation change at constant |a|, and a windowed standard deviation of the RAW AXES catches that at zero cost; the idea names std of |a| as the control, which is the weaker of the two plain rivals. Streams synthesised by concatenating gestures with rest favour any rest detector by construction. The PD detection half is decorative: no frame length at 500 kS/s is given, and this session's demonstrator already runs the plain detector (train on noise, distance-to-winner AUROC), so 'no current report addresses detection' is out of date; a frame map must beat that score. Boundary F1 is new and uncalibrated, as admitted. This is a pipeline, not an improvement to the map.

dropped.title: A DBA finishing pass on the trained map (closing the barycentre question)
dropped.lens: movement / gesture / HAR from wearable sensors
dropped.why_dropped: The win criterion is met by construction: a DBA iteration at frozen winners is a descent step on the within-unit DTW objective that QE measures, so 'QE lower on 8 of 10 seeds' is guaranteed and carries no information; TE will rise, as the batch DBA-SOM already showed; and ARI, read from the Ward cut, is expected to be a wash by the proposer's own account. The project already has two points on this line (re-timing after training: purity up, TE up; batch DBA-SOM: less ordered), and this adds a third with a predictable outcome. It is honestly labelled a closing experiment, not a lever, which under the researcher's rule means it does not earn its own seed-by-seed run. Partly tested, as stated.

dropped.title: Null-model skill scores: permuted lattice and random prototypes make QE, TE and KL fair across map sizes
dropped.why_dropped: The TE null needs no permutations at all: for a random placement the winner and runner-up land on two random cells, so TE_perm = 1 - mean degree/(K-1) exactly (0.167 for 2x2 where 5 of 6 pairs touch, as the metrics report already says; ~0.95 for 10x10 hex). At a fixed lattice it is a constant, so skill_TE is a monotone rescaling of TE and changes nothing at the same size, which the idea admits; across sizes it is a guess that rho(size, skill) lands near 0, and a 2x2 map with TE 0.03 would read skill 0.82 against 0.95 for 10x10, which is not obviously 'fairer' than the raw trap the project already names. The fit-null (K random items as prototypes) is a weaker floor than L11's k-means / DBA ratio, which answers the same cross-size question better. The only genuinely new piece is the route null for KL - QE, and that is a footnote, not an experiment. Pölzlbauer (2004) WDA'04 is real as far as I recall, but it does not supply a size-corrected TE.

dropped.title: U-matrix clarity: ridge contrast, basin count and boundary ratio as the measure of what a person sees
dropped.why_dropped: Ridge contrast R is a data property as much as a map property: a well-ordered map on a continuous cloud has a flat U-matrix and low R, which is correct behaviour, not a fault, so 'R ranks batch > online' is not an expected result but an unsupported prediction (batch's k-means-like end decorrelates neighbours, which can raise or lower top-decile/median link ratios depending on the data). Basin count B(t) is threshold-dependent and is the same question as L5 (how many groups does the map show without labels), answered by a second method. BR (between-class / within-class link height) is the only adjacency-aware class number here and it will track purity closely. For PD the 'technician reads a ridge' use is decorative: the field detection question is L6's, not readability. Ultsch & Siemon (1990, INNC) and Ultsch (2005, U*C) are real as far as I recall.

dropped.title: Heskes' energy at a fixed evaluation radius as a principled single objective (and a redundancy test against KL)
dropped.why_dropped: The 'wins on E by construction' claim is wrong under the project's schedule: the online Heskes-winner SOM does SGD on E(sigma_t) with sigma_t annealed to 0.5, so the finished map minimises nothing at sigma_eval = 1; it is only a clean test if sigma is frozen at sigma_eval for the last passes (or in batch mode). E at sigma = 1 is a neighbourhood-weighted QE (each hex neighbour weighted ~0.61 relative to the winner), i.e. 'do the winner's neighbours also fit', which is likely to correlate with KL above 0.9 on every set; the idea's own redundancy rule would then retire it. Under DTW the energy is not the objective of the warped update, as admitted. Heskes (1999) in Oja & Kaski, Kohonen Maps, pp. 303-315 and Erwin, Obermayer & Schulten (1992, Biol. Cybern. 67) are correctly cited. As a map variant, Heskes' winner is one more point on the order-for-fit curve the project already has (CHAOSOM restarts, floating radius, smooth schedule), with no reason to expect it to beat the smooth-schedule control that already gives the lowest TE.

dropped.title: Compare at equal cost, not equal K: Pareto fronts over sizes and passes in the (alignments, KL) plane with a hypervolume summary
dropped.why_dropped: The experiment cannot change the verdict it targets: the growing DTW-SOM is both cheaper (17% fewer alignments) and better at the same K, so an equal-budget rival is a DTW-SOM with FEWER passes, which can only be as good or worse; the growing map already dominates on both axes. A (cost, KL) front across sizes reproduces the size trap the project already names (KL falls with K, cost rises with K), so the front just rewards spending the budget on units. The hypervolume depends on an arbitrary reference point (relQE 1.5, TE 0.5) and mixes two normalisations. Alignment counts are gameable: the core's LB_Keogh pruning gives identical winners with half the alignments, so cost must be DTW cells or time under the same pruning, which the idea half-acknowledges. The PD device-budget framing is decorative: PD maps of 600 waveforms x 125 points take seconds. 2,400 maps for this is not worth an hour. Zitzler & Thiele (1999, IEEE TEC 3(4)) is the hypervolume reference as far as I recall.

dropped.title: Read the precision budget off the gap before buying any precision
dropped.why_dropped: (1) Half of it already exists in this repository: ns_core.cpp records gap[s] at every step, the full bench cache (5 seeds x 4 sizes x 3 sets, 3,015 rows) carries gap_median and gap_tiny per fit, Section 6d of som_next_steps.Rmd prints 'Contests closer than 1e-6' (0 to 1.7e-4 for every hard-winner variant), and Section 8 already plots the gap histogram against the 2^-23 and 2^-52 lines and reports first_flip and total flips per precision rung. The idea's 'no report has run' is stale. (2) The 'prediction' is not one: #{s : gap_s < c * eps} contains the fitted constant c (the text says 'no free parameter' and then writes c), and the error that flips a contest is not eps but the accumulated error of a 125-term sum plus the drift of M, so c absorbs the physics. (3) Dynamical objection: after the first flip the two runs are different trajectories, and the gaps of the base run say nothing about the contests of the other run; the idea's own numbers show it (0 contests closer than 1e-6, yet 68% of fp32 DTW winners flipped). The only predictable quantity is the first flip, which Section 8 measures directly. (4) Birth and tear margins: the growing map is not in the demonstrator (Section 10) and tearing was closed by the project; measuring their margins needs the old core for a question nobody asked. (5) No measure can move, by the idea's own account, and the researcher asked for improvements. Project anchor checked: the chaotic page's nudge test exists (Section 4) but nudged unit outputs, not prototypes, which the idea does not say.

dropped.title: The precision ladder upward: fp32, fp64, 80-bit, 128-bit, MPFR-256 on the same seed, counting flips and drift
dropped.why_dropped: Already built and run in this repository. next_steps/R/ns_precision.R trains the same seed, start and order in fp32, fp64, fp64 + Kahan, fp80, fp128, fp32 data in fp64 arithmetic and MPFR-256; next_steps/ns_mpfr.cpp does the MPFR loop in C for BOTH Euclid and DTW (mode 6), and train_mpfr() in Rmpfr is the independent check of the Euclid loop; next_steps/cache_quick/precision_8c7e97f7a3e5.rds holds a run (5 x 5, 360 CBF and 600 PD steps, both modes), and Section 8 of som_next_steps.Rmd reports first flip, flips, drift curves at 40 snapshots, QE, TE and seconds per rung with the verdict 'fp64 is the right precision; MPFR is the oracle once per core change, not for training'. The idea's cost section is stale: it says an MPFR DTW oracle 'needs C with mpfr_t and is not worth it' when that file exists and has run. The only increment is more seeds and sizes, for a result the idea itself expects to be null, and the roadmap already lists MPFR training under 'not worth the time'. A double-double DP cell would be a third oracle for a question that has two. 'Certificate' overstates it: agreement with the oracle holds per trajectory (this seed, this order), which Section 8 already says.

dropped.title: DTW path ties are where precision enters: a census of near-tied DP predecessors and the three tie rules
dropped.why_dropped: (1) The DP distance is tie-independent: at a tie the predecessors carry the same cost, so the winner contest, and with it the field unit's mapping, cannot depend on the rule; only the backtraced path can, and the path is used in one place, the training update (Section 3d of the next-steps report says the same). (2) In training the prototype is a continuous fp64 vector after the first pass (M0 is a draw of items, but every unit is pulled in the first wide-radius pass), so an exact predecessor tie needs two different sums of (x_i - m_j)^2 to coincide exactly, which with quantised x and continuous m essentially never happens; the quoted census (0.4% at 12 bits, 3.8% at 8 bits, '200 pairs') was almost certainly item against item, where both operands are quantised, and does not transfer to item-against-prototype alignments. (3) Even where a tie is real, on a flat stretch of the item the tied paths average identical values onto the prototype, so the warp of the plateau is the same under every rule; the rule can only move the entry and exit of a tied block by a point or two, a change of alpha h |dx| in one or two coordinates that the contractive update forgets. (4) Clipping of the real recordings is asserted, not documented: the benchmark describes a free-field microphone in an anechoic chamber and says nothing about saturation. The project's own tie test (benchmark Section 2, sample(0:2) series) checks that R and C++ agree, not that the rule matters. Expected outcome: null within seed spread, which the idea half admits ('small or unknown'). Anchors checked: the tie comment is at ns_core.cpp line 140 as described; Sakoe & Chiba and DBA are standard.

dropped.title: Bit-for-bit reproducibility across builds and machines: a flag matrix, a recorded RNG kind, and a libm-free neighbourhood
dropped.why_dropped: The mechanism is right (GCC contracts a*b+c by default in GNU C++ mode, AArch64 has FMA in the base ISA, libm exp differs across platforms, sample() changed in R 3.6.0, max.col 'first' is exact) and the project's bit-identity checks are indeed all same-machine (benchmark Section 2: 'differences exactly zero', growing_vs_classic Section 4). But it is hygiene, not an experiment: the four-builds x two-machines x ten-seeds matrix answers a question Section 8 has already answered in the only way that matters, a last-bit difference either flips no winner or yields 'one more seed', and the idea's own fallback criterion ('same winners and measures within 1e-6') is already the roadmap's criterion. The libm-free kernel is an algorithm change (compact support, no far pull) proposed for a non-reason: the Gaussian row is computed once per radius value and a 1-ulp difference in exp is exactly the kind of perturbation the chaotic page showed to die out. No measure can move, and neither target application trains on two machines; the field unit maps.

dropped.title: Does the map forget a flip? Perturbation and forced-flip response of the training trajectory
dropped.why_dropped: A finite-time Lyapunov exponent is the wrong quantity for this system. The SOM update is contractive only within one winner assignment; across a Voronoi boundary it is discontinuous, so a perturbation decays as (1 - alpha h) per pull until a contest closer than the perturbation flips, then jumps by alpha h |x - m| regardless of the perturbation's size. The 'exponent' therefore measures the size of the nudge against the gap distribution, not a property of the training phase: the chaotic page found exactly this (nothing below 1e-6, flips within a step at 1e-3) and Section 8's gap histogram explains it. The perturbation-response curves exist and were run: ns_precision.R logs max |M - M_ref| at 40 snapshots per rung and Section 8 plots them; the fp32 curve is the response to a rounding-sized perturbation, with the first flip at step 134 of 1,200, inside the ordering phase, and a final map 'different, not worse', TE within seed spread, which is the ordering-phase case the idea wants to test. The remark that momentum and conscience states would need exporting shows the entry point is more work than claimed. Relevance: only for training on the device, which neither target needs. Anchors: Erwin, Obermayer & Schulten 1992 and Cottrell, Fort & Pages 1998 are real; the project refs are correctly described except that the drift curves have been run, not only coded.

dropped.title: fp16 and bfloat16 training with the swamping test and its three fixes
dropped.why_dropped: fp16 TRAINING matters only for on-device adaptation, which neither target application asks for; the PD field unit maps, and for mapping fp16 is one rung of the downward ladder that roadmap item 5 already names and P6 should run. The outcome of the three fixes is foreseeable: an fp32 master copy leaves fp16 only the contest, and Section 8 already shows that a flipped contest yields 'another seed', so the master copy restores fp64 behaviour by construction; stochastic rounding and a residual accumulator are its known substitutes; bf16 fails by construction. Ten seeds x six rungs x two sizes to confirm the textbook is not worth the time. The swamping arithmetic is right in form (half an ulp of m over alpha h) but 0.4 is the top of the range (0.2 for |m| in 4-8, 0.39 in 8-16); the one-seed probe showed quality unchanged at 2 passes and the idea admits the stall may stay modest at 20. Micikevicius et al. 2018, Gupta et al. 2015 and Kalamkar et al. 2019 are real and correctly attributed.

dropped.title: Statistical precision, not arithmetic: a smaller final learning rate, and why averaging the last pass does not help
dropped.why_dropped: The framing is the best in the batch (the map's imprecision is stochastic-approximation jitter, 1e13 times rounding; that sentence is the answer to the MPFR question and belongs in Section 8's text), but the experiment does not pay. (1) A linear decay to 0.001 instead of 0.01 over the same S steps changes alpha only in the last few percent of the steps, and a prototype's relaxation time is about 1/alpha wins: at alpha = 0.001 that is 1,000 wins per unit, against about 12 wins per unit per pass on the PD stand-in (600 items, 49 units), so the chain never reaches the smaller stationary wobble; it just freezes a little earlier. That is the measured result: 0.2% QE on 7/10 Euclid seeds, below the project's 'margin that matters', and worse on 4/5 DTW seeds because DTW prototypes are still re-timing in the last pass. (2) The averaging explanation is wrong as stated: the radius is already fixed at 0.5 for the last quarter of training (r < 1 is used as 0.5), so nothing 'still shrinks'; the average lags because the window (one pass, about 12 wins per unit) is shorter than 1/alpha, i.e. the iterates are not stationary. Polyak-Ruppert needs a flat tail of many times 1/alpha wins per unit, and a flat tail with averaging is a batch step: the project's batch SOM, which already wins QE and loses TE. The whole space collapses onto a known trade-off. (3) Three alpha_end values on all sets, three sizes, two distances and ten seeds is a full benchmark of CPU for a gain at the seed-noise floor, and the project's best map (growing DTW-SOM) is in the family it hurt. Polyak & Juditsky 1992, Robbins & Monro 1951 and Kohonen 2001 are real; the project never varied alpha_end, as stated.

tiers.rationale:
Five experiments, each one table at 4x4 / 7x7 / 10x10 (3x3 / 4x4 on BasicMotions) x 10 seeds, with every project measure (QE, EV, TE, KL, TP, purity, ARI, NMI, used units, alignments, seconds) plus the new columns the verdicts name; QE/EV only within one representation or distance (lesson 6). The ids are merged exactly as the verdicts asked.

(1) Reading and statistics. L10-honest-stats first, on the cached benchmark (zero compute): with 10 seeds the sign test gives p = 0.34 for 7/10 and 0.11 for 8/10, so several 'helps' verdicts in the summary will turn into 'undecided', and the 30-seed rerun on the three near-margin cells (PD growing DTW-SOM vs DTW-SOM on ARI, CBF TE, GunPoint KL) settles them; KL and QE get a relative margin, Friedman runs per family. Then PD8-heldout-reading + L7-heldout-confusion + PD6-novelty-score + L6-novelty-detection + L9-confidence-calibration as ONE held-out section: same maps, same pool, fold draw fixed per seed and reused by every variant; cache rebuilt with folds only for the four live variants (online SOM, DTW-SOM, growing DTW-SOM, batch SOM); margin score d2 - d1 with the label-disagreement flag instead of KL (KL flags folds, not class ambiguity); per-unit thresholds by a parametric fit, FA rates of 5-10% not 1% (the 99th percentile of 24 items is the maximum); the leave-one-class-out novelty test as the real 'new kind of discharge' question; ARI(k) for k = 2..8 as a curve; named same-session held-out, paired with PD1's rescaling as the transfer proxy; leave-subjects-out for movement. Why first: the benchmark's own Limits say 'ARI and NMI rest on one choice', the project found part of DTW's PD gain was in reading the map, per-class precision/recall and FAR at fixed recall are the numbers a PD report is judged by, and this can re-rank every variant at the cost of retraining four maps.

(2) The PD representation ladder, gated by PD4's diagnostic table (dominant frequency and -3 dB bandwidth per pulse, by class; an hour; published regardless; the whitening arms themselves are tier B). PD2-tf-features (run with and without the two loudness columns; features standardised on the training 600; a supervised ceiling per representation so ARI is read against what the space allows; drop W if it is the sensor bandwidth for every class), PD3-envelope-spectrum (envelope-only and spectrum-only arms so the reader sees which channel carries the ARI; per-class onset-delay histogram to flag the lab timing leak; 64 or 125 envelope points; eps = noise-class envelope RMS), and L11-transformed-series-distances (the model-free 5-number descriptor map: log RMS, spectral centroid, bandwidth, decay time to 1/e, onset time; envelope map; log-spectrum map after a shift with a Hann window; scattering and cepstrum dropped; prototype ringing-frequency and decay-time error against the class median as the PD analogue of CBF's timing error). Why: on pd_acoustic the Euclidean SOM read with DTW nearly matched the DTW-SOM, so the classes are nearly separable without elastic alignment once the right view is taken; the 5-number map is the strongest plain control any time-domain variant must beat on this set; training needs no alignments.

(3) The loudness question, same seeds and sizes, one table: PD1-amp-channel (shape-only, shape + lambda * log-peak channel, asinh; plus the loudness-only 1-D control on log peak alone that no report has; FAR on rescaled noise as the number where shape-only can lose; the log-peak channel's share of the squared distance reported per lambda; note that z-DTW was alignment-only and is not a prior shape-only result), L3-cosine-correlation-shape-loudness (correlation after the best global shift within +-5%, i.e. SBD with a loudness coordinate; loudness as log10 RMS or peak of the raw pressure; renormalisation-off must reproduce the project's SOM on z-scored inputs; lambda chosen on seeds 11-15, tested on 1-10; the lambda = 0 ARI is the transferable part and lambda -> inf the artefact), and P8-asinh-companding-bits reduced to the knee: p0 in {noise RMS, 0.3, 1, 3, 10 mPa} on the real pd_acoustic, Euclid and DTW, 7x7 and 10x10, per-class purity at fixed size, the ADC depth and share of full-scale samples reported first (the bit-depth half moves to P6 in tier C). Why: asinh(1e4) is about 9.9, the microphone distance and sources are fixed in the lab, and a high ARI that is a loudness meter will not transfer; three lines of code.

(4) Shift, not warp. PD5-shift-not-warp (arm a: onset alignment once, zero shift for 'no onset found', same detector applied to held-out pulses; arm b1: lag-bounded Euclidean with the shift-then-update rule and a stated edge rule; arm b2: SBD labelled scale-free and read against PD1's shape-only arm, never against the asinh maps) + L6-sbd-one-global-shift (max shift +-2% and +-5%, i.e. up to 8 samples, not 20%; the distribution of s* per class on the trained map as the diagnostic). Controls: DTW-SOM at 10% and at 2-3% (one line; the 5% window on pd_acoustic exists in the cache on 3 seeds), plain SOM, every map read with its own distance, with DTW and with the shift distance (the project's reading lesson). Why: the pulses are triggered by the current pulse so the only misalignment is a few samples of propagation and trigger jitter; lesson 2 says DTW or not depends on the data; the probable result 'SBD = tiny-band DTW = Euclidean on pd_acoustic' is still the number that says whether to drop the elastic family on PD and points at (2). On the gesture sets the shift-only arm is the control that shows how much of DTW's gain is segmentation jitter.

(5) The one map change and the movement input layer. L4-heskes-winner: h_ij / sum_j h_ij per unit, squared distances (for DTW the cumulative cost before the root), lowest-index tie-break so R and C++ agree to the last bit; run as the L1-free-energy verdict specifies, start radius x0.5 and x0.25 against the plain SOM / DTW-SOM at the same smaller radius AND at the default, with the smooth-schedule fixed map (TE 0.036 on CBF) as the bar; log the winner-not-nearest share next to the chaotic units' share and the rim-unit share; win = TE and KL lower on >= 7 of 10 seeds with QE within seed noise, a TE-for-QE trade is the CHAOSOM result and does not count. Why: the metrics report shows a start radius of 0.5-1 gives TE near 0.2 against 0.03 at the default, the tearing lab showed the smaller start gives the fit gain at that order cost (lesson 5), and an energy-consistent winner is the one cheap mechanism that attacks the order cost directly; 15 lines, zero extra alignments. L8-multivariate-dtw-dependent-vs-independent with L1-dtw-independent-adaptive reduced to DTW_D vs DTW_I (adaptive arm dropped: DTW_I <= DTW_D always, so the ratio carries no signal without labels): order of work is the UEA .ts loader, DTW_D, the stacked per-channel z-scaled Euclidean control (DTW_D at band 0 must equal it bit for bit), then DTW_I with the inter-channel path-lag diagnostic; z-scale per channel over the data set, never per series; BasicMotions (80 series) at 3x3 / 4x4 only, UWaveGestureLibrary at 4x4 / 7x7 / 10x10; read every map with its own distance and with one common distance. Why: the project's gesture sets are Z-axis cuts, so the movement goal cannot be addressed at all without this; it is the missing input layer, not a SOM improvement, and the report should say so.

Built after tier A has produced its tables, because each either depends on an A result or rides on A's infrastructure (folds, the diagnostic table, the N x N matrix).

Elastic alignment, conditional on A(4)'s s* histogram and A(2)'s ladder showing that alignment still carries PD information, or run on the gesture sets regardless: L5-soft-dtw-gradient-update and L2-soft-dtw-free-energy are the same mechanism from two lenses and become ONE experiment: hard winner (LB_Keogh kept), column-normalised expected alignment E in the update so gamma -> 0 gives the project's along-path mean within 1e-9 (the raw gradient is n_j times the project's step, i.e. the pinched points), gamma relative to the median gap between best and second-best path, controls = DTW-SOM, widening-window DTW-SOM and growing DTW-SOM (both already cut the CBF timing error 3.6 -> 2.0), QE/TE/KL judged in hard DTW, new columns = alignment entropy per update and the prototype's ringing amplitude relative to the series it wins; the pre-test (share of prototype points whose E mass splits across ringing cycles on a trained map; skip below ~10%) comes before the 150 lines. L9-step-pattern-slope-constraint targets the measured pinch at its source (longest run of copied points 1.0 -> 12.8 as the window widens; events bunch, timing error 4.4 vs 0.8): verify against dtw::dtw(step.pattern = symmetricP1) unnormalised, report the longest run per pattern next to the CBF timing error, run CBF, Trace and the gestures first and PD last (on 125-point pulses with a 12-sample band P1/P2 is nearly the diagonal and converges with L6-sbd). Supervised finishing, needs A(1)'s folds: L7-lvq-finetune and L10-1nn-ceiling-lvq as one: the 1-NN DTW ceiling first on every set (a number the project never had), per-class DBA-template 1-NN at the same K as the honest same-budget rival (K random items is too weak), OLVQ1 / LVQ3 with a window, rate 0.03 -> 0, prototypes left with zero items counted, held-out accuracy and macro-F1 in their own columns and never merged with the unsupervised verdicts; alignment ratio stated as N_train / K (5-20x on the lab set, not 100x); Somervuo & Kohonen (1999) cited as the source of DTW-LVQ.

Reading-step results, no new training loop: L10-ustar-cluster-extraction and L5-groups-from-data as one 'k from data' table per cached map: Ward with oracle k, Ward with k by criterion, basins of the plain U-matrix, basins of U*, item-level silhouette, DBSCAN-style clustering on the items as the no-map rival; 20x20 maps first on pd_acoustic, Synthetic Control and colours (U*C is built for emergent maps; on 25-100 units it will mostly fail, which is part of the result); Pareto radius from the pairwise item distances; deterministic flood order; dead units along walls reported; labelled a reading-step result (lesson 6). This is the honest successor of tear-then-rejoin: the walls are found after training with no effect on the pull, which is where cutting lost (tearing never beat a smaller start radius; pieces vs Ward found the same clusters).

Measures: L11-fit-ratio-kmeans with DBA k-means (batch DTW-SOM at radius 0, same start) as the DTW floor and R's kmeans with the same start under Euclid, K capped at N/5, G may fall below 1 with a medoid floor; L2-trust-continuity in a unit-level version (prototypes on exact lattice coordinates, no ties) and a BMU-level version with the tie share, plus the one control the growing-map verdict never had: a plain SOM trained from a random start on the grown map's FINAL lattice (som_online_cpp takes any lattice distance matrix g), which separates the growth process from the outline that made TP disagree; L8-seed-stability by retraining the live variants with the per-item bmu stored (the cache holds scalars only), AMI for units, ARI at the true k for groups, bootstrap over seeds, and the per-item co-association wobble map that would show a technician which waveforms are assigned unreliably.

Schedule and structure: L12-online-then-batch-hybrid with the switch when the radius reaches 1 (not at 60%), batch floor swept over 0.5 / 0.75 / 1, DBA capped at one iteration per pass with alignments counted, random start for all four maps, batch phase parallelised over units with a fixed item order so the result is bit-identical across thread counts; the probable result 'the floor, not the hybrid' still converts the batch verdict from 'worse order' to 'worse order because the radius shrank to 0'. L3-stop-prune-ghsom trimmed to stop + prune: no birth while the worst unit's accumulated error is below tau1 x the map mean for a full pass (tau1 on seeds 11-15), prune a unit with zero wins over a full pass after growth stops, no refill; controls = growing DTW-SOM retrained at the stopped size and the fixed DTW-SOM at that size, everything at matched used units; GHSOM children dropped (N/K ~ 6 items per unit cannot populate them); the practical PD result is a size and a count without hand tuning. L8-median-relational-som as the online median SOM (prototypes are real series, K alignments per new pulse, so it fits a detector; relational only as a cross-check and with the share of negative distances reported): the N x N DTW matrix computed once per band with a symmetric band and the upper triangle stored, reused by every seed, size and variant (179,700 alignments once against ~1.2M per online run at K = 100); it also supplies L10-ustar's Pareto radius, L5's item silhouette and PAM as a quantisation bound; collisions and dead units counted; QE judged in plain DTW.

Distances and preprocessing: PD4-whiten collapsed to one spectral whitening filter with two spectra (mean pulse spectrum; noise PSD by Welch over the 150 noise pulses), floored, zero-phase, the 125 x 125 covariance dropped, the asinh knee re-set to the whitened noise RMS, whiten-then-asinh and asinh-then-whiten as two arms; run only if A(2)'s diagnostic says the ringing is the sensor, since dividing by a class-mixed mean spectrum erases class differences. L1-manhattan-huber as Huber only (pure L1 reported as the delta -> 0 end, not tuned), delta tied to the running median residual so it follows the learning rate, the share of steps where the Huber winner differs from the squared-cost winner as the wash diagnostic (below a few percent it is a wash by construction), QE in L2 for all maps, and the spliced-pulse / clipped-peak stress test on 10% of items that matches the robustness claim; read next to L3's lambda sweep, because on asinh data Huber mostly down-weights loudness; the Manhattan arm already in the next-steps cache ('a different contest, not a better one' on the stand-in) must be confirmed on the real pd_acoustic judged in its own distance before L1 is chosen for anything. L2-magnitude-gravity-frame as a preprocessing matrix, not a SOM improvement: only the UWave rows count as evidence, the synthetic rotation rows are a labelled sanity check (the generator rotates by construction, so |a| wins there by construction), and the PD amplitude arm lives in A(3). L3-magnification-control: the zero-cost diagnostic first (units per class and hit-histogram entropy on the cached pd_acoustic, Pebble and Wiimote maps; with balanced classes the units may already be proportional and no m can move the Ward cut); only then alpha_r = alpha (K f_r)^m clipped to alpha, the rho = 1 arm against DeSieno's conscience, and the negative-m detection arm on a deliberately imbalanced resample (600 noise, 50 per PD class) with per-class recall from the Ward cut against the plain SOM on the same resample; rho_hat from log(units per class) against log(class mass) across imbalance levels.

Long shots, or null results the user asked for, each worth one small run. physics_bridge:
### Which physics is exact, which is a picture

The SOM has three objects a physicist can touch: the winner assignment (a discrete configuration), the prototype update (a descent step) and the lattice coupling h (an interaction). An idea maps exactly when a physical quantity is identical to one of these and a limit of it reproduces the project's code to floating-point tolerance; otherwise it is a picture, and pictures add knobs.

**Soft-DTW is the free energy over alignment paths (exact; survived as L5 and L2).** Hard DTW is the ground-state energy over monotone paths through the banded cost matrix; soft-DTW_gamma = -gamma log sum_paths exp(-cost/gamma) is the Helmholtz free energy of the Boltzmann distribution over the same paths at temperature gamma, and its gradient with respect to the cost matrix is the expected path E (Cuturi & Blondel 2017). The DTW-SOM today backtracks one ground state and averages the series points matched to each prototype point; the thermal version replaces that single configuration by the ensemble average x~_j = sum_i E_ij x_i / sum_i E_ij. In the loop: a forward soft-min recursion (log-sum-exp, banded), a backward pass for E, column normalisation of E so that gamma -> 0 returns the project's along-path mean within 1e-9 (not bit for bit: the raw gradient sum_i E_ij (m_j - x_i) is n_j times the project's step, exactly the pinched points), the hard winner kept so LB_Keogh pruning survives, and gamma set relative to the median gap between the best and second-best path. The honest limit: with ringing periods of 10-25 samples inside a 12-sample band, an ensemble over two paths one cycle apart averages opposite phases, the smearing the DTW-SOM exists to avoid. Hence the pre-test on a trained map (share of prototype points whose E mass splits across cycles) before any code, and one new column, the entropy of the alignment distribution per update.

**Energy and temperature on the winner (exact).** Erwin, Obermayer & Schulten (1992) showed the online SOM with the nearest-unit winner has no energy function in the continuum; Heskes (1999) showed that c = argmin_r sum_s h_rs ||x - w_s||^2 restores one, so training becomes stochastic gradient descent on E = sum_x min_r sum_s h_rs d^2(x, w_s). Graepel, Burger & Obermayer (1997) add a temperature: F = -(1/beta) sum_i log sum_r exp(-beta E_r(x_i)), responsibilities P(r|x), the SOM as the beta -> infinity limit, and phase transitions at which the map unfolds dimension by dimension. But the radius schedule is already an annealing, and the soft update weight sum_r P(r|x) h(r,s) is a data-dependent wider radius: QE up, TE down, the CHAOSOM trade in a new coat. The change that earns a run is the hard one: one line in the winner search, h normalised per unit (otherwise rim units with fewer neighbours are favoured), squared distances, lowest-index tie-break, and two new columns, the winner-not-nearest share and the rim share. Run it at start radius x0.5 and x0.25 against the plain map at the same radius and at the default: the tearing lab showed the small start buys fit at an order cost; if an energy-consistent winner removes that cost (kinks are local minima of E), the pair beats the default on QE and TE together, which only the growing map has done. The chaotic-units failure (winner not nearest) is its negative image.

**Magnification exponent (exact in 1-D, approximate on the hex lattice).** Ritter & Schulten's Fokker-Planck stationary state gives a prototype density q proportional to p^(2/3); Bauer, Der & Herrmann (1996) steer the exponent with a density-dependent rate. In the loop: alpha_r = alpha (K f_r)^m with f_r the unit's running hit frequency, clipped to alpha; m = 0 is the plain SOM, m > 0 moves toward equal usage (DeSieno's conscience is the rival), m < 0 gives rare items more units, a one-line base-rate knob for field detection. Honest points: BDH's density proxy is prototype spacing, not within-unit spread, so rho-hat is read from log(units per class) against log(class mass) across resampled imbalance levels; and the zero-cost diagnostic (units per class on the cached maps) comes first, since with 150 balanced pulses per class no m may be able to move the Ward cut.

**Optimal transport (exact formula, metaphorical label).** The 1-D Wasserstein-2 distance between unit-mass profiles is the L2 distance between quantile functions, and its barycentre moves peaks instead of fading them as the Euclidean mean does. In the loop: normalised Hilbert envelope, cumulative sum, quantile function on a fixed u grid, then the ordinary Euclidean SOM on those coordinates, prototypes read back by inverting Q, loudness as a separate coordinate. "Transport" is a label; the testable claim is that a shifted event costs linearly and a prototype's ramp moves rather than smears, and the CBF timing error is its one honest reading. Polarity is lost, so it is a tier C probe.

**Renormalisation (one exact piece, mostly a speed-up).** Block-averaging in time is a renormalisation step and FastDTW's coarse-path projection bounds the fine path; no fixed point or universality is used. Train on the envelope at 32 points, upsample, continue in a corridor around the coarse path, and count DTW cells against a compute-matched DTW-SOM. Plain 4x decimation aliases PD ringing; the envelope is the coarse level, and the envelope-only map is itself a PD finding.

**Pictures that did not survive.** Lattice springs are a final-radius sweep (metrics report: final radius 1 lowers TE, raises QE, KL lowest near 1). Griffith fracture for tearing: once the pull follows graph distance, cutting a link changes h for every pair whose path used it, so the "energy released" is not a pairwise term, three knobs replace the median rule's one, and the prior stands at 0 wins in 216 comparisons. Replica exchange: the replicas are deterministic descents, not samplers of exp(-beta E), so detailed balance does not apply and the product is best-of-R by KL. Heat kernels equal the Gaussian up to boundary terms on a full lattice; momentum is a rescaled learning rate; Kuramoto coupling needs a phase channel the data lack.

**Precision as temperature.** The online SOM is a stochastic process whose fluctuations are set by alpha and the item order, the seed; the repository's Section 8 ladder shows fp64, 80-bit, 128-bit and MPFR choosing the same winner at every step of the same seed. Rounding sits many orders of magnitude below that seed noise, so refining it is cooling a gas by polishing the thermometer. MPFR is the oracle once per core change; the precision question with a payoff runs downward, to 8-bit integer mapping on the field unit.
