If a model-free 5-number map matches the DTW-SOM's ARI, the whole elastic family is moot on this data set; that is the most useful single number you can get.
- **Settle the loudness question in the same tables** (PD1, L3, the asinh knee of P8): asinh(1e4) is about 9.9, so four decades of loudness become a ~10-unit feature and the map may be a loudness meter that will not transfer out of the anechoic chamber. The loudness-only 1-D map (log peak, Ward k = 4) is the control no report has; the lambda = 0 and lambda -> infinity ends are the finding, whatever the middle does.
- **Shift, don't warp** (PD5, L6-sbd): PD pulses are trigger-aligned, so a lag-bounded shift of +-2-5% is the physically right invariance. The DTW-SOM at a 2-3% band is a one-line control (the 5% window already sits in the cache) and the per-class histogram of the best shift decides whether elastic alignment has anything left to do on PD.
- **The one cheap change to the map itself worth running now** is Heskes' energy-consistent winner (L4, 15 lines, zero extra alignments, h normalised per unit) at half and quarter start radius, against the plain map at the same radius *and* at the default. Lesson 5 says a smaller start buys fit at an order cost; this is the pairing that could beat the default on QE and TE together, which only the growing map has done. Its soft, annealed version is the CHAOSOM trade in a new coat, so hard arm first.
- **Movement needs an input layer before any variant:** the UEA loader plus dependent vs independent multichannel DTW (L8-multivariate; L1-dtw's adaptive arm dropped), with DTW_D at band 0 equal to the stacked Euclidean SOM bit for bit as the correctness check; then the 1-NN DTW ceiling and per-class held-out confusion with leave-subjects-out splits (L10-1nn, L7); slope-constrained steps (L9) and open ends (L6-open-end) after.
- **Physics that maps exactly:** soft-DTW is literally the free energy over alignment paths (L5 / L2), Heskes' winner and the annealed assignment are an energy and a temperature on it (L4 / L1-free-energy), the magnification exponent is Ritter & Schulten's stationary density (L3-magnification), 1-D transport has a closed form (L12-wasserstein). Springs, Griffith fracture, replica exchange, heat kernels and momentum were dropped as pictures that re-parametrise the final radius or the learning rate.
- **Manhattan and MPFR are already answered with numbers in the repository** (som_next_steps Section 8: fp64, 80-bit, 128-bit and MPFR choose the same winner at every step, so MPFR is an oracle, not a training precision; Manhattan reads "a different contest, not a better one" on the stand-in and needs confirming on the real pd_acoustic in its own distance). Tear-and-rejoin got no survivor: the ageing, Griffith and jigsaw variants were dropped against the 0-of-216 prior; its honest successor is finding the walls *after* training on the U-matrix (L10-ustar, tier B), which leaves the pull untouched.

gaps.title: Tear-then-rejoin by data support (GNG edges) was dropped, contradicting the host report and the user's request
gaps.why_it_matters: The user asked for tear-then-rejoin explicitly; the summary's own untested list names 'cutting by data support as Incremental Grid Growing does' and 'neural gas'; and /home/user/novl_SOM/som_next_steps.Rmd Section 3b and roadmap item 3 (Section 9) already promise 'Growing neural gas edges on the SOM lattice' as the surviving tear-and-rejoin. The synthesis dropped the 'ageing' variant against the 0-of-216 prior, but that prior is about tearing by link LENGTH; an edge born when two units are winner and runner-up of an item and killed when no item has done so for a_max steps is a different mechanism (a reason for every tear and every rejoin, no length threshold). When ideas.json is injected into the report, Section 9's box will promise an experiment the tiers do not contain.
gaps.suggested_fix: Reinstate one tier B item: GNG edges on the hexagonal lattice (edge set initialised to the lattice, aged every step it is not the winner-runner-up pair, removed at age a_max, re-created on co-occurrence; the pull follows graph distance over live edges with the 0.5 floor). Controls: the growing DTW-SOM with its fixed lattice AND the plain SOM at the smaller start radius (the control that beat every tearing variant). Measures: QE, TE and KL on the live graph (state that TP is undefined without a lattice), pieces as in the tearing lab, on the three-blob set where tearing helped and on the 18 sets where it did not; one knob a_max swept on seeds 11-15. Add plain neural gas (Martinetz 1993, rank-based neighbourhood, no lattice) as the same-schedule quantisation floor next to L11-fit-ratio's k-means.

gaps.title: The window per unit for the growing map (listed untested, promised as roadmap item 4) is absent
gaps.why_it_matters: The project's lesson 2 is that the DTW band is a property of the data (CBF 0.24 to 0.92 ARI from 10% to 20%; solar I-V better at 5%), the growing DTW-SOM already keeps a per-unit floating radius, and som_next_steps.Rmd Section 9 item 4 names the per-unit band with its reason (trigger-aligned pulses get a narrow band, gestures a wide one). The kept list has no growing-map item that touches the alignment at all.
gaps.suggested_fix: Tier B: each unit carries its own Sakoe-Chiba band set from the items it won in the last pass (e.g. the 90th percentile of |s*| from the best-shift histogram that PD5/L6-sbd compute anyway, floored at 2 samples, capped at the global band); births inherit the parent's band. Control: the growing DTW-SOM with the global band at 5%, 10% and 20%, same seeds and sizes; report DTW cells (not alignments) as the cost, the per-class band distribution, and the CBF timing error and PD ARI judged in plain DTW at 10%.

gaps.title: Kept ideas already run in the repo's demonstrator are presented as new
gaps.why_it_matters: The rule is that ideas already tested in the project must be marked as such. som_next_steps.Rmd Sections 6-7 (code in /home/user/novl_SOM/next_steps/R/ns_maps.R and ns_core.cpp) already ran cosine, correlation, SBD, soft-DTW, Manhattan, the clipped (Huber-like) pull, conscience, deterministic annealing on the Euclidean and DTW maps, momentum, torus vs rectangular sheet, trustworthiness/continuity and a noise-trained AUROC detector with per-class AUROC, at four sizes with every measure, 5 seeds, on synthetic stand-ins. The kept items L3-cosine-correlation, L6-sbd, L5-soft-dtw, L1-manhattan-huber, L1-free-energy-winner, the conscience arm of L3-magnification, L2-trust-continuity and L6-novelty-detection carry no such mark, and the synthesis cites only Section 8 (precision) and the Manhattan verdict.
gaps.suggested_fix: Add a status field to every idea ('untested', 'project: tested, verdict ...', 'demonstrator: stand-in, 5 seeds, Section 6/7 verdict ...'), quote the demonstrator's seed counts as the prior for each, and phrase the tier A work for these as 'repeat on the real pd_acoustic, GesturePebbleZ1/ShakeGestureWiimoteZ and the UEA sets with 10 seeds' (which is roadmap item 1). Note explicitly that the demonstrator's PD stand-in is asinh-companded with onset jitter of 4 us, so its Manhattan and precision verdicts are stand-in results, not closed questions.

gaps.title: The torus is dropped although it is the cleanest rim control for Heskes' winner and TP, is listed untested, and is already coded
gaps.why_it_matters: A(5) normalises h per unit because rim units have fewer neighbours, TP is known to react to the map outline, and L2-trust-continuity exists partly to be 'immune to the outline'. The torus removes the rim altogether with one lattice distance matrix (som_online_cpp takes any g; ns_maps.R already builds hex, rect and torus). Its only data-side reason (mains phase) is conditional, but as a control it is unconditional.
gaps.suggested_fix: Add the torus as one control row in A(5) (Heskes' winner on the torus needs no per-unit normalisation; compare the rim-share column against the sheet) and in the L2-trust-continuity/TP table (TP on torus vs sheet isolates the outline effect). Control: the rectangular sheet, same seeds, judged on KL and trust rather than TE because four neighbours count more runner-ups as errors.

gaps.title: The win rule contradicts the honest-statistics item it sits next to
gaps.why_it_matters: Tier A(1) states that 7 of 10 seeds gives p = 0.34 and 8 of 10 gives p = 0.11 under a two-sided sign test, yet A(5) defines the Heskes win as 'TE and KL lower on >= 7 of 10 seeds', tier B uses 'beat on the three blobs and stay level', and the growth-stop rule and others use bare counts. A reader applying A(1) will reject A(5)'s own success criterion. The same section asserts 'DTW_D at band 0 equals the stacked Euclidean SOM bit for bit', which will fail spuriously because the per-cell sum over channels then over time rounds differently from a sum over the stacked vector.
gaps.suggested_fix: State one decision rule once, in L10-honest-stats, and make every tier reference it: with 10 seeds a win is paired Wilcoxon p < 0.05 with the Hodges-Lehmann CI excluding zero (equivalently >= 9/10 by sign test); 7-8/10 is 'undecided' and triggers the 30-seed rerun; 'level' is an equivalence verdict with a stated margin (e.g. QE within 2%, TE within 0.01). Replace 'bit for bit' by 'within 1e-12 relative, or summed in the same order'.

gaps.title: The novelty detector has no non-SOM control
gaps.why_it_matters: PD6 and L6-novelty-detection score only SOM variants (as does Section 7 of som_next_steps.Rmd, where the Euclidean alarm scored below 0.5 on corona because a Euclidean distance is mostly loudness). A PD engineer's first detector is a peak-amplitude or RMS threshold; a statistician's is the 1-NN distance to the noise pool. Without them a map AUROC of 0.9 cannot be read as a gain.
gaps.suggested_fix: Add three control rows to every detection table: (a) peak amplitude / log RMS threshold, (b) 1-NN distance to the noise training pool under the same distance as the map, (c) a one-class Gaussian/Mahalanobis on PD2's descriptor features; all with ROC AUC, F1 at fixed FAR and FAR at fixed recall; keep the per-class AUROC so corona-below-0.5 remains the diagnostic. The map must beat (b), which is the same-distance, no-map rival, seed by seed.

gaps.title: The real held-out pool (850 untouched waveforms per class) is never used
gaps.why_it_matters: The benchmark states that pd_acoustic's 150 waveforms per class were 'drawn at random from 1000'. The synthesis builds folds inside the 600, accepts FA rates of 5-10% because 'the 99th percentile of 24 items is the maximum', and rations 30-seed reruns. With 3400 untouched waveforms, held-out per-class precision/recall, per-unit thresholds at 1% FAR, false alarms per 1000 triggers, leave-one-class-out novelty and seed reruns all become cheap and honest, and the 'which 150' draw becomes a nuisance seed that should vary with the training seed.
gaps.suggested_fix: Train on the 600 (or a fresh 150-per-class draw per seed), test on the remaining 850 per class; report FAR at 1% with real counts, and the ARI/purity of the held-out assignment next to the training-set ARI so the optimism of every earlier verdict is measured. Ask whether the 1000 are from one session; if several, use session as the fold for the transfer question.

gaps.title: Consensus over seeds (evidence accumulation) is skipped, though it is the cheapest ARI gain and the honest 'replica' product
gaps.why_it_matters: Ten cached maps per cell already exist. A co-association matrix over the ten Ward cuts, cut at k, is a zero-training ensemble that routinely beats any single run on ARI (Fred & Jain 2005, Strehl & Ghosh 2002, unverified). L8-seed-stability uses co-association only as a wobble diagnostic, and replica exchange was dropped to 'best-of-R by KL' without naming consensus as the alternative.
gaps.suggested_fix: Tier A reading-step item, no training: consensus clustering of the items from the 10 (or 30) cached maps per cell, ARI/NMI against the labels; controls = the single map with the lowest KL, the median-seed map, and a consensus of 10 k-means (Euclid) / 10 DBA k-means (DTW) runs so the gain is attributed to ensembling rather than to the map; per-item co-association entropy as the wobble column it already planned.

gaps.title: Movement has no engineer's baseline, unlike PD's 5-number map, and P6 misses its published precedent
gaps.why_it_matters: For PD the synthesis insists on a model-free descriptor control (PD2, L11). For movement every table pits DTW variants against the raw stacked Euclidean SOM only. The HAR field's control is the windowed feature vector (per-axis mean, sd, energy, dominant frequency, inter-axis correlations, magnitude statistics); and uWave (Liu et al. 2009, unverified), the source of UWaveGestureLibrary, is an integer DTW on acceleration quantised to 33 levels, i.e. a published version of P6-fixed-point-manhattan on the very data set proposed.
gaps.suggested_fix: Add a per-series feature-vector Euclidean SOM as the control row of every movement table (same seeds, sizes), plus a supervised ceiling on those features; cite uWave as the precedent and prior for P6 and run P6's integer DTW against it. Optionally one unsupervised transform from time-series classification (MiniRocket random convolution kernels, Dempster et al. 2020, unverified) into the Euclidean SOM, control = the raw stacked SOM, as the movement analogue of L11.

gaps.title: The one case where precision matters by construction is missing from the fp64/MPFR answer: raw pressure without asinh
gaps.why_it_matters: Every precision row (repo Section 8 and PD11) uses asinh-companded data whose values span about 10 units, so fp32 and fp64 agree. On raw pressure over four decades, a loud sample squared ((1e4 mPa)^2 = 1e8) swallows a 1 mPa pulse's whole squared contribution (1) below fp32's epsilon (6e-8 x 1e8 = 6): fp32 squared-Euclidean cannot see the quiet classes at all, fp64 can. This is the honest positive answer to 'fp64 data', explains why asinh was needed, and ties to P8's knee.
gaps.suggested_fix: Add a 'raw pressure, no companding' row to the PD11 ladder (fp32 vs fp64 vs MPFR; winner agreement, per-class purity, and the share of squared-distance mass carried by the loudest 5% of samples), expecting it to be the only precision-dependent result; report the ADC bit depth of the recordings next to fp32's 24-bit mantissa before any 8-bit floor claim.

gaps.title: PRPD / mains phase, the field's standard PD feature, is never asked about
gaps.why_it_matters: Power engineers classify PD sources by phase-resolved patterns (phase angle, charge, count); no uploaded report mentions the mains phase, and the repo's torus reason is conditional on it. If the recordings carry the AC phase and/or inter-pulse times, that single circular channel may separate corona from void and gap discharges better than any waveform distance, and it is the control a waveform-SOM must beat; if not, the report should state the limit.
gaps.suggested_fix: One question to the data owner (Havránek et al. 2026): is the phase angle, apparent charge and timestamp of each pulse available? If yes: add phase as a (cos, sin) pair or a torus axis, and the per-source PRPD histogram SOM as a control row; if timestamps exist, pulse-sequence-analysis features too. If no, add a one-line limit in the PD section.

gaps.title: The measure list and the size grid of the new tables do not match the project's
gaps.why_it_matters: The digest says every project measure must appear: tier A names QE, EV, TE, KL, TP, purity, ARI, NMI, used units, alignments, seconds and omits the timing error (CBF), spread (colours), pieces and % above optimum. Tier A also fixes 4x4 / 7x7 / 10x10, whereas the cached earlier reports use 5x5, 8x8, 10x10 and 20x20 (and the demonstrator its own four sizes); QE, KL and purity change with units, so cross-report comparison breaks unless the sizes coincide.
gaps.suggested_fix: Publish one measure matrix: set-specific measures appear whenever their set is run (timing error on CBF, spread on colours, pieces whenever edges are edited, TSP stated out of scope), and keep CBF and colours as sanity sets in every tier A table because they catch smearing and shape loss. Choose the size grid from the sizes the caches already hold (at least 5x5 / 8x8 / 10x10, plus 20x20 for U*-matrix work) and name the figure set per experiment: maps per size as a tabset, one measure across sizes, variant vs control seed by seed, and the DT table with every measure and a size filter, as Sections 5-6 of som_next_steps.Rmd already do.

gaps.title: L9-step-pattern does not name Derivative DTW as the project's prior attack on the same pinch
gaps.why_it_matters: Derivative DTW (Keogh & Pazzani 2001) was built precisely to remove singularities, i.e. the pinch of many points onto one, and the project tested it: 'no gain in general, one clear win on the solar I-V curves'. Slope-constrained step patterns target the same failure; without DDTW as a row the reader cannot tell whether a slope constraint adds anything to what the project already measured.
gaps.suggested_fix: Add the project's DDTW variant as a control row in the L9 table, report the longest run of copied points and the CBF timing error for DDTW as well, and mark L9 'related to a tested variant' with the solar I-V set included because that is where the prior variant won.

gaps.title: No ingredient is ported into the growing DTW-SOM, the project's best map
gaps.why_it_matters: The user's favourite and the project's winner on QE, TE and KL together is the growing DTW-SOM, yet the kept list gives it only structure items (stop/prune, streaming) and a lattice control. The repo's Limits section says 'nothing above says how an ingredient behaves while a map grows', and roadmap item 2 promised soft-DTW births as a soft barycentre and the annealed winner during growth.
gaps.suggested_fix: State one rule: any ingredient that wins on the fixed map in tier A or B (Heskes' winner, SBD or shift-then-update, soft-DTW barycentre births, the loudness channel, the per-unit band) is re-run inside the growing DTW-SOM, its births using the ingredient's own distance or barycentre, against the plain growing DTW-SOM at matched used units and alignments; same seeds, both sizes.

overall: The brainstorm is strong where it reads maps, counts seeds honestly and builds the PD representation ladder, and its physics bridge is exact where it claims to be; but it has quietly regressed against the report it will be embedded in, dropping the GNG edges, window per unit and torus that som_next_steps.Rmd Sections 3b and 9 promise, presenting nine ideas the demonstrator already ran as new, contradicting its own sign-test arithmetic in the Heskes win rule, and never using the 850 untouched waveforms per class that make its held-out and detection programme cheap. Add the plain non-SOM detector and the movement feature baseline, the raw-pressure precision row, the consensus-over-seeds reading and the port-into-the-growing-map rule, and the roadmap covers everything the user asked for on both targets.

lens_summaries.physics: Physics / statistical mechanics / dynamical systems lens, chaos excluded (the project showed twice that chaos adds nothing over its plain clock). I weighed every candidate on one question: is the mapping to SOM objects exact (an energy, a partition function, a density law, a graph operator) or a metaphor? Exact mappings, in order of promise for the two targets: (1) a temperature on the winner assignment (Heskes' energy, STVQ free energy) and (2) soft-DTW as a free energy over alignment paths both turn the project's hard argmin lines into expectations and reduce to the current online SOM / DTW-SOM at zero temperature, so the control is the gamma=0 or beta=infinity limit of the same code; (3) magnification control (Ritter-Schulten density law, Bauer-Der-Herrmann local learning rate) is the only candidate with a knob for class loudness/rarity, which is the PD detection problem in one line; (5) the elastic net gives the lattice a real spring energy, and with DTW the spring between neighbouring prototypes shares timing along the map, which the re-timing experiment showed is what breaks order. Partly exact: (6) replica exchange over the soft-winner temperature (exact Metropolis test on Heskes' energy; the project's 'restarts with the best kept' is its crude form), (7) the graph heat kernel as neighbourhood (exact on any link graph; differs from the geodesic Gaussian only where the graph is irregular, so it matters only for grown, torn and rejoined maps), (10) the circular SOM update, which is Kuramoto's coupling form and is exact for phase or angle channels but not applicable to the present pd_acoustic set, which records no AC phase. Metaphors made testable: (4) Griffith fracture, where the stored strain energy is read from the cross terms of Heskes' energy and cracks propagate from existing cuts, which is the one tearing rule the project has not tried against its radius x0.5 control; (8) renormalisation as coarse-to-fine in TIME (envelope first, ringing later) and a tree-structured winner search, mostly a cost saver; (9) momentum, which I rank last and pair with Polyak iterate averaging as the cheaper rival. Set aside: Langevin noise with cooling (folded in as the noise control of idea 1: the online SOM's item order already is Langevin noise with alpha as temperature; a second heater would repeat the CHAOSOM finding), the Fokker-Planck view on its own (folded into idea 3 as the empirical magnification exponent, a new diagnostic for the report), and pure multi-scale map growth (already the growing SOM). Common risk across the lens: every annealing candidate is a second schedule on top of the radius schedule, so each test must include a radius-matched plain control (start radius x1.5 and x0.5, final radius 0.5 and 1) or a gain will be a wider-radius effect in disguise, exactly what CHAOSOM restarts turned out to be. Precision note: all log-sum-exp quantities here are stable in fp64 with the usual max-subtraction; none of these ideas needs MPFR. Suggested first runs: ideas 1 and 3 on pd_acoustic and the gesture sets (cheap, no new alignments), idea 2 on CBF at window 20% and the Wiimote shakes, idea 8 wherever alignment counts dominate.
lens_summaries.distances: LENS: distances and alignments inside the SOM. The project's rule for a new distance d(x, m) is already the right one and generalises: the online update is a gradient step on d with the alignment held fixed, m <- m - alpha*h*grad_m d(x, m). For the project's DTW that gives the along-path mean (Somervuo & Kohonen); the analogues are: L1 -> sign/median step (Huber: clipped step); Minkowski-p -> |r|^(p-1) sign(r); cosine/correlation -> Kohonen's dot-product step with the prototype projected back onto the unit sphere; Mahalanobis/whitened -> the plain step in whitened coordinates (prototypes read back by W^-1); soft-DTW -> the backward-pass gradient = a mean over ALL series points weighted by the expected alignment (gamma -> 0 recovers the project's map bit for bit); SBD -> shift the series by the best global lag, then the plain step; TWED/MSM/ERP/LCSS -> matched pairs pull, gaps and deletions leave the prototype point alone; multivariate DTW_D -> one path moves all channels of a prototype point together, DTW_I -> one path and one mean per channel; slope-constrained DTW -> the same along-path mean but each prototype point receives at most two series points (no pinch); transformed views (envelope, log-spectrum, cepstrum, scattering, physical parameters) and 1-D Wasserstein (quantile functions) -> the plain Euclidean step in the transformed space, with the prototype read back by the inverse transform or, where there is none, by the unit's medoid series (the growing map's birth rule reused as a read-out). Lower-bound pruning changes nothing in the update and must give identical maps. Two traps carry over from the project: QE/EV/KL are only comparable within one distance (judge a new distance by ARI/NMI/purity, TE, used units, timing error, and by QE in the control's distance), and a distance that helps in training usually helps in READING the map too, so every new distance should also be tried as the mapping/clustering distance of the plain SOM (the project's 'read with DTW' check on pd_acoustic). What fits what: PD pulses are trigger-aligned damped oscillations whose class cues are ringing frequency, decay time and loudness (4 decades, asinh). DTW with a 10% band can warp the frequency away, so the best bets for PD are the ones that remove only jitter and phase and keep frequency/decay/loudness: SBD one global shift (idea 6), spectral/envelope/physical views (11), whitening (4), a shape-plus-loudness split (3), soft-DTW for the ringing phase-slip (5) and slope constraints (9); L1/Huber (1) is a robustness gain for the noise class. Multi-channel movement data has no counterpart in the project at all (every series tested is univariate), so dependent vs independent multivariate DTW (8) is the one large expected gain there, with slope constraints (9), TWED's soft warping penalty (7) and the cosine-plus-vigour split (3) as plausible seconds. LB pruning in the training winner search (10) is speed only, and the Minkowski/Chebyshev sweep (2) is most likely a clean negative result that settles the Manhattan question. Every idea names the plain control it must beat seed by seed (same start, same order of items, same schedule, three map sizes, 10 seeds) and carries a limit (delta -> inf, gamma -> 0, nu -> 0, p = 2, lambda = 0, epsilon -> inf) at which it must reproduce that control to the last bit, which is the correctness check the project likes.
lens_summaries.pd: PD measurement engineering lens. The project treats a partial-discharge (PD) pulse as a generic 125-point series: asinh(p/1 mPa), Euclidean or DTW, map read by Ward with k = 4 on the training items. A PD engineer would first ask three questions the benchmark cannot answer yet, each a cheap seed-by-seed experiment with the existing code: (1) is the map sorting pulses by LOUDNESS or by SHAPE (the four lab sources differ by four decades of loudness, which asinh keeps as a ~10-unit feature; loudness does not transfer to the field, where it is distance and air absorption) - idea PD1; (2) is the ringing the SENSOR or the SOURCE (every pulse carries the same microphone/chamber impulse response; if all classes peak at the same frequency, Euclidean and DTW both spend their attention on the sensor) - the diagnostic in PD4; (3) is the residual timing jitter of trigger-aligned pulses a SHIFT or a WARP (a 10% Sakoe-Chiba band is about one ringing period at 40 kHz, so DTW can map one cycle onto the next and erase the frequency/decay differences that separate sources; the project's own finding that the Euclidean map READ with DTW nearly matched the DTW-SOM says the gain is small and at the reading step) - PD5. Second, make DETECTION the goal with its own measures: distance-to-map as a novelty score with per-unit thresholds and the Kaski-Lagus path as a topology-aware second score (PD6), and a held-out reading with per-class precision/recall and false-alarm rate on noise plus a U-matrix cut instead of Ward k = 4 (PD8); the Zenodo record's unused 850 pulses per class are a ready held-out pool, and the detection measures (AUC, FAR at 95% recall) must be added next to QE/EV/TE/KL/TP/purity/ARI/NMI/used/alignments. Third, bring the representations PD practice trusts as yardsticks: Contin's T-W map plus pulse-shape features (PD2) and the envelope + magnitude-spectrum split (PD3), both shift-tolerant so a plain Euclidean SOM may match DTW at a tenth of the cost. Fourth, make the growing map serve detection by changing its birth rule (by hits or by novelty rather than by error, PD7). PRPD phase channels are the strongest PD discriminator but only testable if the record carries phase (PD9). Lower priority: soft-DTW against cycle-skipping of ringing prototypes (PD10) and a falsification test of fp32/fp64/MPFR (PD11: no gain expected; the ADC and asinh bound the useful precision; float32 may even be the speed win). On Manhattan: after asinh the large excursions are already compressed, so an L1 winner with a sign (median) update is expected to be a wash; it is included as a one-line arm inside PD4 rather than as its own idea. General caution from this lens: the lab data (fixed geometry, anechoic chamber, loudness separated by decades) are easier than the field, so an AUC near 1 for every method is likely on raw asinh data; the amplitude-rescaling transfer test of PD1 should become standard so that detection comparisons are not saturated. The Havránek et al. (2026) Zenodo record cited in the benchmark could not be found online and is cited here as the project cites it.
lens_summaries.structure: Lens: the map's structure and its learning rule, read through the project's own evidence. Three project facts drive the list. (1) The growing DTW-SOM won fit and order together, which says resolution should follow the data's error: hence a growth-stop rule, idle-unit pruning, GHSOM children, and GNG-style lattice links that are born and die by data support instead of by link length. (2) Tearing lost to a half start radius because it weakened the pull unevenly DURING ordering, so every structural change proposed here acts after the ordering phase (edge ageing only once the radius is below 1; jigsaw and U*-matrix after training) and must beat the half-radius map seed by seed, not just the plain one. (3) Part of DTW's gain was in reading the map, so the two cheapest large gains are in the reading step: U*-matrix basins with k found from the data, and LVQ fine-tuning when labels exist; both change no training measure and must be reported in their own columns. On the learning rule, two cheap principled changes to the winner (Heskes' neighbourhood winner; DeSieno's conscience) are exactly the sanity controls the chaotic-units experiment lacked, and both must log the share of steps the winner was not the nearest unit. Neural gas and the median/relational SOM change the prototype representation (rank neighbourhoods; real series and an arbitrary dissimilarity matrix); the relational route is the practical door to multi-channel movement data and to Manhattan or soft-DTW point costs without touching the training loop, and it makes the N x N matrix a one-off cost shared by every seed, size and variant. An online-then-batch hybrid with the 0.5 radius floor tests whether batch's disorder was the batch or the floor. Honest expectation: small gains on QE/TE from most structural tweaks (the project's history says so), larger gains on alignments, dead units, cluster count, seed-to-seed spread and held-out classification. Every idea is sized for the project's protocol: 5x5 / 7x7 / 10x10 maps (20x20 where N >= 480, e.g. pd_acoustic), 10 seeds with the same start items and order, the full measure table (QE, EV, TE, KL, TP, purity, ARI, NMI, used/dead units, timing error, alignments, seconds), and a win = better on at least 7 of 10 seeds by a margin above seed noise, against the plain rival that does the same job. Verified references are marked; the rest are from memory and marked (unverified).
lens_summaries.movement: Movement / gesture / human-activity recognition from wearable or handheld sensors. What the project has: single-channel maps only. Its gesture sets (GesturePebbleZ1, ShakeGestureWiimoteZ) are the UCR Z-axis-only cuts, GunPoint is one coordinate, and the demonstrator being built in next_steps/ already covers Manhattan/Chebyshev/Minkowski/cosine/correlation, SBD, soft-DTW, dependent multi-channel DTW, deterministic annealing, conscience, Huber clipping, momentum, torus lattice and fp32-to-MPFR precision. So this lens does not repeat those. It brings what multi-axis movement data force on a SOM and what the project has never asked: how channels are aligned (dependent vs independent DTW, adaptive choice), which invariances to buy and at what price (orientation via magnitude or a gravity frame, or a Kabsch rotation per pair; speed via DTW, a learned per-unit band, or time-warp augmentation for the cheap Euclidean map; amplitude via normalisation, which should go the opposite way on PD where loudness is a class cue), sloppy segmentation (open-begin/open-end DTW), continuous streams (a two-level trajectory map that also gives PD a field detector), a map that keeps learning (births, deaths, per-unit rates), and the supervised ceilings the reports never show (1-NN DTW, LVQ fine-tune). Data notes: the UCR AllGestureWiimoteX/Y/Z sets are shuffled independently per axis (confirmed on their Zenodo pages) and cannot be stacked into 3-channel series; use UWaveGestureLibrary (UEA, 3 synchronised axes, 8 gestures), Cricket (6 channels, two wrists) and the demonstrator's synthetic 3-axis gestures. PLAID is appliance current signatures, not gestures: closer to the PD side. Every idea names the plain control that does the same job without the new ingredient, to be run seed by seed with the same start and order, over 4x4/7x7/10x10 maps, reading QE/EV/TE/KL/TP/purity/ARI/NMI/used units/alignments/seconds, plus two new measures where the problem needs them (boundary F1 for streams, held-out accuracy for the supervised ceiling). Ideas already tested in the project are marked; DBA is included only as a closing experiment with an honest small expectation.
lens_summaries.evaluation: The project's seven numbers (QE, EV, TE, KL, TP, purity, ARI/NMI, plus used units, timing error, spread, alignments, seconds) are a strong in-sample toolkit, and the reports already know their traps. Four gaps remain, and they are exactly the gaps that block a fair comparison across map sizes and a verdict for the two target applications. (1) Size-fairness: QE, KL and purity fall or rise with K because any K prototypes do; TE is cheap on coarse maps. The cure is not a new score but a null model per map: the same prototypes with lattice positions permuted (kills order, keeps fit) and K prototypes drawn from the items (keeps size, kills learning), giving skill scores near 0 for an untrained map and near 1 for a perfect one at any size; the project's random-unit purity line and relQE are special cases. (2) Out-of-sample and task-level numbers: every current measure is computed on the training items; a labelled map used as a classifier on held-out folds (per-class confusion, macro-F1), a noise-trained map used as a novelty detector (ROC AUC, false alarms per 1000 noise triggers) and a confidence read from distance-to-winner (error-detection AUROC, coverage-accuracy, ECE) are what PD monitoring and gesture recognition actually consume, and held-out accuracy is size-fair by construction. (3) Statistics: with ten seeds, 6/10 wins has sign-test p = 0.75, 8/10 p = 0.11, 9/10 p = 0.02; the benchmark's ~1,176 (variant, measure, data set) cells would yield ~59 'wins' at p < 0.05 by chance; paired Wilcoxon with a Hodges-Lehmann difference and CI, Holm/FDR within families, Friedman-Nemenyi across data sets and an equivalence verdict with the project's own margins cost nothing and will probably retract some claimed wins. (4) Stability: the spread over seeds is the spread of a number, not of the map; ARI between the groupings of different seeds says whether a variant gives the same map twice, which a monitor needs. Secondary additions with a clear mechanism: trustworthiness/continuity and the co-ranking curve (rank-based on items at a chosen k, immune to the map outline that confuses TP, and able to show whether tearing trades continuity for trustworthiness), Heskes' energy as a principled single objective to test against KL for redundancy, U-matrix ridge contrast and basin count as the measure of what a human sees, silhouette/Davies-Bouldin to let the map choose the number of groups (ARI at data-chosen k), a fit ratio against k-means/k-medoids at the same K with a DTW version of EV, and equal-cost Pareto fronts across sizes (the fair rival of a growing map that saves 17% of alignments is a plain map given the same alignments). A protocol for accepting any new measure: it must be flat in K for the plain SOM where the raw measure is monotone (Spearman |rho| < 0.3 vs > 0.9), it must agree with a held-out task metric across the 14 variants, and any verdict it changes must carry a sign-test or Wilcoxon p below 0.05 on the paired seeds. Suggested table design: one row per (variant, size, data set, distance), column groups raw | null | skill per measure, dropdowns for size and judging distance, cells coloured only when the 95% CI of the paired difference against the family baseline excludes zero, and a tooltip with wins/n, p, Hodges-Lehmann difference and d_z. Priority by value per hour: honest statistics (zero compute, changes the report today), held-out confusion plus the novelty detector (the application), null-model skill plus the fit ratio (the across-sizes wish), seed stability (free from the cache), then trustworthiness/continuity, calibration, U-matrix, Heskes' energy, groups-from-data and equal-cost fronts.
lens_summaries.numerics: Numerical precision lens, with measurements rather than guesses. The project's next_steps module already contains a four-rung C++ ladder (fp32 / fp64 / 80-bit / 128-bit, template train_T<T> in /home/user/novl_SOM/next_steps/ns_core.cpp), a Neumaier-compensated sum option, a per-step 'gap' record (d2 - d1) / d1 and an Rmpfr 256-bit reference loop (/home/user/novl_SOM/next_steps/R/ns_precision.R), but no cache exists, so none of it has been run. I ran it on the synthetic PD stand-in (make_pd: 600 series x 125 points, asinh scale, 4 classes), 7 x 7 map, seed 1, 2 passes (scripts /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-novl-SOM/669d37d7-4892-59ef-aba7-1e2d40ab701e/scratchpad/precision_probe.R to precision_probe5.R; fp16 rung in a scratch copy ns_core_fp16.cpp, the project file untouched). Findings. (1) fp64 is exact for the map's purpose: against fp128, zero winner flips in Euclid, Manhattan and DTW, prototype drift 5e-15; 80-bit drift 2e-16; Kahan/Neumaier changes no winner and no bit of drift; fp32 STORAGE of the data (24-bit significand) flips nothing (drift 1e-7) because ADC data carry fewer bits than that. (2) fp32 ARITHMETIC flips nothing in the pointwise SOMs over 5 seeds (measures identical to 3 decimals), but flips 585-816 of 1,200 winners in the DTW-SOM (first at step 134), final winner agreement 6-39%: a different map of the same quality (QE, TE, purity within the seed spread). Cause, measured by a DP census: 0.078% of band cells have their two best predecessors within 2^-23 (about 2.4 cells per 125 x 25 alignment), none within 2^-52, 15% within 2^-10; with 12-bit / 8-bit quantised data 0.4% / 3.8% of cells are EXACT ties, where the tie rule, not precision, decides the warp. So precision enters DTW through the path choice, not through the winner contest (no winner contest closer than 1e-6 in 1,200 steps; 8% closer than 1e-3; median gap 1.5% Euclid, 5% DTW). (3) fp16 arithmetic (_Float16, GCC 13): every trajectory diverges from step 4, winner agreement 0-10%, quality still within seed spread at 2 passes, but Manhattan's TE doubles and 27.7% of last-pass coordinate updates are below half an ulp of the prototype (6.3% in fp32: the far units with h ~ 1e-10) - the update-swamping that freezes an exponential moving average; fixes are an fp32 master copy, stochastic rounding or a residual accumulator. (4) Data bit depth: asinh-scaled PD at 8 bits (48 distinct values per series) gives the same QE/TE/purity/ARI as fp64 over 5 seeds; 6 bits slight; 4 bits QE +1.3%; raw linear 12 bits QE +0.8%; raw linear 8 bits collapses (QE 22.3 vs 12.2, purity 0.63 vs 0.81): asinh is a mu-law companding law and the knee at 1 mPa decides which classes keep waveform shape. (5) Reproducibility: -O2 -ffp-contract=off versus -O3 -march=native -ffp-contract=fast (51 FMA and 16 AVX instructions emitted) gave bit-identical prototypes for Euclid and DTW on this x86-64 machine; R 4.3.3's max.col(ties.method = 'first') has no tie tolerance (verified at 1e-15); the remaining cross-machine hazards are libm exp (the one non-correctly-rounded operation in the loop), FMA on ARM64, OpenMP reduction order in any future batch code, and R's sample() kind (changed in R 3.6.0). (6) Cost: 80-bit x3-5, 128-bit x25 (DTW) to x82 (Euclid); Rmpfr 256-bit Euclid 0.48 s per step, about 96 min for one 20-pass PD map at 7 x 7 and about 3.3 h at 10 x 10; DTW in Rmpfr is infeasible (an R loop over ~3e9 cells); an MPFR DTW oracle must be C with mpfr_t (x100-300, 1-2 h per PD map); double-double cells give fp128-like accuracy at x3-5 and are the practical oracle. (7) The 'very precise SOM' the user imagines is limited by the schedule, not by arithmetic: a prototype coordinate wobbles by 0.044 (Euclid) / 0.012 (DTW) within the last pass, 10^13 times the rounding; Polyak-Ruppert averaging of the last pass made QE WORSE on 10/10 Euclid seeds (iterates still converging), while a final learning rate of 0.001 instead of 0.01 lowered QE and KL on 7/10 Euclid seeds (QE 10.707 to 10.682, KL 19.56 to 19.21) and was mixed on DTW (QE worse 4/5, TE and KL better 3/5). Verdict for the user: MPFR is a one-off certificate, not a training mode; fp64 is already exact; the direction that matters for a field PD device is DOWN (int8-int16 Manhattan/SAD with exact integer DTW, 8-bit asinh data), with fp64/fp128 as the oracle; all numbers above come from the synthetic stand-in at one map size and must be repeated on the real pd_acoustic, CBF, GunPoint and the gestures set, over sizes and seeds, as the project does.
